title.en: Volume 151 Biographies 38: Xuetalahai, Gao'er, Wang Yi, Wang Yu, Zhao Di, Di Shun, Wang Shan, Du Feng, Shi Mobeidieer, Jia Talahun, Ao Dunshi Ying, Tian Xiong, Zhang Badou, Zhang Rong, Zhao Tianxi

sentences.zh: 薛塔剌海

translations.literal: Xue Talahai
translations.idiomatic: Xue Talahai

sentences.zh: 薛塔剌海，燕人也，剛勇有志。

translations.literal: Xue Talahai was a man of Yan; he was fierce and brave and ambitious.
translations.idiomatic: Xue Talahai came from the Yan region. Bold and resolute, he was a man of strong purpose.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，太祖引兵至北口，塔剌海帥所部三百餘人來歸，帝命佩金符，為砲水手元帥，屢有功，進金紫光祿大夫，佩虎符，為砲水手軍民諸色人匠都元帥，便宜行事。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year, Taizu led troops to Beikou; Talahai led more than three hundred men of his command to submit. The emperor ordered him to wear a gold tally and made him marshal of artillery and naval forces. For repeated merit he was promoted to Golden Pacifier Grand Master of the Palace, granted a tiger tally, and appointed grand marshal over artillery sailors, military and civilian personnel, and craftsmen of every category, with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year, when Genghis Khan marched to Beikou, Talahai brought over three hundred troops under his command. The emperor had him wear a gold tally and named him marshal of artillery and naval forces. After repeated victories he was promoted to Golden Pacifier Grand Master of the Palace, given a tiger tally, and appointed grand marshal over artillery sailors, troops and civilians, and artisans of all kinds, with full discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 從征回回、河西、欽察、畏吾兒、康里、乃蠻、阿魯虎、忽纏、帖里麻、賽蘭諸國，俱以砲立功。

translations.literal: On campaigns against the Huihui, Hexi, Qincha, Uighur, Kangli, Naiman, Arughu, Huchan, Tielima, Sailan, and other states, in every case he won merit with artillery.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against the Muslim lands, Hexi, the Qipchaqs, the Uighurs, Kangli, the Naimans, Arughu, Huchan, Tielima, Sailan, and other realms, winning distinction with his artillery in each.

sentences.zh: 太宗三年，睿宗引兵自洛陽渡河，塔剌海由隴右假道金、商，遂會師于鈞州三峰山，敗金師。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taizong, Ruizong led troops across the river from Luoyang; Talahai took a detour through Longyou via Jin and Shang, then joined forces at Sanfeng Mountain in Junzhou and defeated the Jin army.
translations.idiomatic: In Ögedei's third year, Prince Tolui led an army across the Yellow River from Luoyang while Talahai came by way of Longyou through Jin and Shang. They united at Sanfeng Mountain near Junzhou and routed the Jin forces.

sentences.zh: 四年，破南京及唐、鄧、鈞、許諸州，取鄢陵、扶溝。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he stormed Nanjing and the prefectures of Tang, Deng, Jun, and Xu, and captured Yanling and Fugou.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he took Nanjing and the prefectures of Tang, Deng, Jun, and Xu, along with Yanling and Fugou.

sentences.zh: 四月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the fourth month.
translations.idiomatic: He died that April.

sentences.zh: 子奪失剌，襲為都元帥，南攻江淮，有功。

translations.literal: His son Duoshila inherited the post of grand marshal, attacked the Jiang-Huai region in the south, and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Duoshila succeeded him as grand marshal, campaigned south against the Jiang-Huai country, and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 歲庚戌，卒。

translations.literal: In the gengxu year he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the gengxu year.

sentences.zh: 弟軍勝襲，憲宗八年，從世祖攻釣魚山、苦竹崖、大良平、青居山，破重慶、馬湖、天水，賜以白金、鞍馬等物。

translations.literal: His younger brother Junsheng inherited the post; in the eighth year of Xianzong he followed Shizu in attacks on Diaoyu Mountain, Kuzhu Cliff, Daliangping, and Qingju Mountain, stormed Chongqing, Mahu, and Tianshui, and was granted white silver, saddles and horses, and other goods.
translations.idiomatic: His brother Junsheng took the command. In Möngke's eighth year he followed Kublai Khan in assaults on Diaoyu Mountain, Kuzhu Cliff, Daliangping, and Qingju Mountain, captured Chongqing, Mahu, and Tianshui, and received gifts of silver, saddles, horses, and the like.

sentences.zh: 中統三年，李璮叛濟南，又以砲破其城。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled at Jinan; again he took the city with artillery.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhongtong year, when Li Tan rebelled at Jinan, he again reduced the city with his artillery.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，從圍襄陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan he followed in the siege of Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 he joined the siege of Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 三月卒。

translations.literal: He died in the third month.
translations.idiomatic: He died that March.

sentences.zh: 丞相阿朮欲以千戶劉添喜攝帥府事，子四家奴，年方十六，請從軍自效，帝壯而許之。

translations.literal: Chancellor Aju wished to have chiliarch Liu Tianxi act as regent of the marshal's headquarters; his son Sijianu, just sixteen years old, asked to join the army and offer his service; the emperor admired this and approved.
translations.idiomatic: The chancellor Aju wanted the chiliarch Liu Tianxi to administer the marshal's headquarters. Sijianu, only sixteen, asked to serve in the army himself. The emperor was impressed and granted his request.

sentences.zh: 八年，始襲父爵。

translations.literal: In the eighth year he first inherited his father's title.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he formally inherited his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 十年冬十二月，襄、樊未下，四家奴立砲攻之，明年正月，襄陽守呂文煥降。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month of winter in the tenth year, Xiang and Fan had not yet fallen; Sijianu set up artillery to attack them; in the first month of the following year the Xiangyang defender Lü Wenhuan surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month of the tenth winter year, while Xiangyang and Fancheng still held out, Sijianu deployed artillery against them. The next first month the Xiangyang commander Lü Wenhuan surrendered.

sentences.zh: 繼從丞相伯顏南伐，十月，至郢州，先登。

translations.literal: Thereafter he followed Chancellor Bayan on the southern campaign; in the tenth month they reached Yingzhou, and he was first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He then followed Chancellor Bayan's southward campaign. In the tenth month they reached Yingzhou, where he was first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 師既渡江，四家奴自鄭州下沿海諸城堡，至建康。

translations.literal: After the army had crossed the Yangtze, Sijianu descended from Zhengzhou along the coastal fortresses to Jiankang.
translations.idiomatic: Once the army had crossed the Yangtze, Sijianu advanced from Zhengzhou down the coastal strongpoints as far as Jiankang.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授武節將軍。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Martial Integrity General.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he received the rank of Martial Integrity General.

sentences.zh: 六月，與宋將夏貴戰于峪溪口，奪其船二百餘艘。

translations.literal: In the sixth month he fought with the Song general Xia Gui at Yuxikou and seized more than two hundred of his ships.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth month he battled the Song general Xia Gui at Yuxikou and captured over two hundred of his vessels.

sentences.zh: 十一月，屠常州。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month he slaughtered Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month Changzhou was put to the sword under his command.

sentences.zh: 十二月，取蘇州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth month he took Suzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth month he seized Suzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，攻鎮巢。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he attacked Zhenchao.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he assaulted Zhenchao.

sentences.zh: 七月，圍揚州，守臣李庭芝棄城走，追獲之。

translations.literal: In the seventh month he besieged Yangzhou; the defending official Li Tingzhi abandoned the city and fled, but was pursued and captured.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month he besieged Yangzhou. The defender Li Tingzhi fled the city but was overtaken and taken.

sentences.zh: 九月，進階懷遠將軍，將兵平浙東諸郡。

translations.literal: In the ninth month he was advanced to Far-Reaching General and led troops to pacify the prefectures of eastern Zhejiang.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month he was promoted to Far-Reaching General and marched to subdue the prefectures of eastern Zhejiang.

sentences.zh: 從征福建灤江，與宋兵力戰，破之，獲戰艦千餘艘。

translations.literal: On the Fujian campaign at Luan River he fought hard with Song forces, routed them, and captured more than a thousand warships.
translations.idiomatic: Campaigning in Fujian at the Luan River, he fought the Song forces fiercely, broke them, and took more than a thousand warships.

sentences.zh: 十六年，進階鎮國將軍，鎮揚州。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was advanced to Nation-Securing General and garrisoned Yangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he was made Nation-Securing General and stationed at Yangzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改為萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was changed to the rank of ten-thousand-household commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was redesignated a myriarch (ten-thousand-household commander).

sentences.zh: 高鬧兒

translations.literal: Gao Nao'er
translations.idiomatic: Gao Nao'er

sentences.zh: 高鬧兒，女直人。

translations.literal: Gao Nao'er was a Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Nao'er was of Jurchen descent.

sentences.zh: 事太祖，從征西域；

translations.literal: He served Taizu and followed campaigns in the Western Regions;
translations.idiomatic: He served Genghis Khan and campaigned in the Western Regions;

sentences.zh: 復從闊出太子、察罕那演，連歲出征，累有功，授金符，緫管管領山前十路匠軍。

translations.literal: again he followed Crown Prince Kuochu and Chaghan Nayen, campaigning year after year with accumulated merit; he was granted a gold tally and made overall supervisor of artisan troops of the ten circuits before the mountains.
translations.idiomatic: he later followed Crown Prince Kuochu and Chaghan Nayen on campaigns year after year, winning repeated honors. He received a gold tally and was put in overall charge of artisan troops of the ten circuits north of the mountains.

sentences.zh: 歲己未，憲宗憫其老，命其子元長襲其職，從世祖渡江攻鄂，還鎮隨州。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year Xianzong took pity on his age and ordered his son Yuanzhang to inherit his post; he followed Shizu across the river to attack E, then returned to garrison Suizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year Möngke, noting his age, had his son Yuanzhang succeed to his post. Yuanzhang crossed the Yangtze with Kublai Khan to attack Ezhou, then returned to garrison Suizhou.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，移鎮季陽。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to garrison Jiyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 he was transferred to garrison Jiyang.

sentences.zh: 五年，從元帥阿朮修立白河口、新城、鹿門山等處城堡，圍襄樊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year he followed Marshal Aju in building fortresses at Baihekou, Xincheng, Lumen Mountain, and other places, and besieged Xiang-Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year he joined Marshal Aju in constructing fortresses at Baihekou, Xincheng, Lumen Mountain, and elsewhere to besiege Xiangyang and Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 七年，充季陽軍馬緫管。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he served as overall commander of Jiyang army and horse forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was made overall commander of Jiyang military forces.

sentences.zh: 十年，從攻樊城，先登。

translations.literal: In the tenth year he followed the attack on Fancheng and was first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year he joined the assault on Fancheng and was first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從渡江，鼓戰艦上流，與宋人戰，殺三百餘人，奪其船及鎧仗，以功賜虎符，陞宣武將軍。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the crossing of the Yangtze, drove warships upstream, fought the Song, killed more than three hundred men, and seized their ships and armor and weapons; for merit he was granted a tiger tally and promoted to Manifest Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he crossed the Yangtze with the main force, drove his warships upstream against the Song, killed over three hundred men, and captured their ships and arms. For this he received a tiger tally and was promoted to Manifest Martial General.

sentences.zh: 進兵丁家洲，與宋臣孫虎臣等大戰，殺五百餘人，奪其船及鎧仗無筭；

translations.literal: Advancing to Dingjiazhou, he fought a great battle with the Song officials Sun Huchen and others, killed more than five hundred men, and seized their ships and armor and weapons beyond counting;
translations.idiomatic: Pressing on to Dingjiazhou, he fought a major engagement with the Song minister Sun Huchen and others, killing more than five hundred and seizing untold numbers of ships and arms;

sentences.zh: 敗夏貴于焦湖。

translations.literal: he defeated Xia Gui at Jiao Lake.
translations.idiomatic: he then routed Xia Gui at Jiao Lake.

sentences.zh: 從征常州，先登。

translations.literal: On the Changzhou campaign he was first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At Changzhou he was again first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 又攻杭州。

translations.literal: He also attacked Hangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He took part in the assault on Hangzhou as well.

sentences.zh: 宋平，護送宋太后至京師。

translations.literal: When the Song was pacified, he escorted the Song empress dowager to the capital.
translations.idiomatic: After the fall of the Song he escorted the Song empress dowager to Dadu.

sentences.zh: 以功進懷遠大將軍、萬戶。

translations.literal: For merit he was advanced to Grand Far-Reaching General and made a myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: For these services he was promoted to Grand Far-Reaching General and made a myriarch.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，領軍二千，從太子脫歡征交趾、追襲交趾世子于大海口，奪其戰艦以還。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he led two thousand troops, followed Crown Prince Togan on the campaign against Annam, pursued the Annamese heir at the Great Sea mouth, seized his warships, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he led two thousand men under Crown Prince Togan against Annam, pursued the Annamese crown prince to the open sea, captured his fleet, and returned.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，陞安遠大將軍、季陽萬戶府萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was promoted to Grand Pacifying-General of the Distant and made myriarch of the Jiyang Myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he rose to Grand Pacifying-General of the Distant and became myriarch of the Jiyang headquarters.

sentences.zh: 是年夏，復以兵追襲交趾世子于海之三叉口，與敵軍合戰，中毒矢而死。

translations.literal: That summer he again led troops to pursue the Annamese heir at the sea's three-forked mouth, engaged the enemy in battle, and died of a poisoned arrow.
translations.idiomatic: That summer he again pursued the Annamese crown prince to the triple mouth of the sea. In the engagement he was struck by a poisoned arrow and died.

sentences.zh: 王義字宜之，真定寧晉人，家世業農。

translations.literal: Wang Yi, courtesy name Yizhi, was a native of Ningjin in Zhending; his family for generations practiced farming.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi, styled Yizhi, came from Ningjin in Zhending. His family had farmed the land for generations.

sentences.zh: 義有膽智，沉默寡言，讀書知大義。

translations.literal: Yi had courage and wisdom, was taciturn and spoke little, and in reading understood great principles.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi was brave and shrewd, sparing of speech, and in his reading grasped what mattered morally.

sentences.zh: 金人遷汴，河朔盜起，縣人聚而謀曰：「時事如此，吾儕欲保全家室，宜有所統屬。」

translations.literal: When the Jin people moved the capital to Bian, bandits arose in the lands north of the Yellow River; the people of the county gathered and deliberated, saying: "The times being thus, if we wish to preserve our households, we ought to have some leadership."
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin court moved to Bian, banditry spread across the Hebei plain. The men of the county met and said, "Times are desperate. If we mean to keep our families safe, we need someone to lead us."

sentences.zh: 乃相與推義為長，攝行縣事，尋號為都統。

translations.literal: Thereupon they together raised Yi as chief, who acted in the county affairs, and soon styled him commander-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: They chose Wang Yi as their head. He administered county affairs provisionally and soon took the title of commander-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 太師、國王木華黎兵至城下，義率衆，以寧晉歸焉。

translations.literal: The Grand Tutor and King Muqali's army reached the city; Yi led the multitude and submitted Ningjin.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Tutor and King Muqali's army reached the city, Wang Yi led the people and surrendered Ningjin.

sentences.zh: 入覲太祖，賜駿馬二匹，授寧晉令，兼趙州以南招撫使。

translations.literal: He entered audience with Taizu, who granted him two fine horses and appointed him magistrate of Ningjin and concurrently pacification commissioner south of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He had an audience with Genghis Khan, who gave him two fine horses and appointed him magistrate of Ningjin and pacification commissioner for the region south of Zhao.

sentences.zh: 是時兵亂，民廢農耕，所在人相食，寧晉東有藪澤，周回百餘里，中有小堡曰瀝城，義曰：「瀝城雖小而完，且有魚藕菱芡之利，不可失也。」

translations.literal: At that time there was military chaos and the people had abandoned farming; everywhere men ate one another. East of Ningjin was a marshland more than a hundred li in circuit; within it was a small fort called Licheng. Yi said: "Though Licheng is small it is intact, and it has the advantages of fish, lotus root, and water chestnuts—we must not lose it."
translations.idiomatic: War had disrupted farming and people were starving; in places men resorted to cannibalism. East of Ningjin lay a marsh more than a hundred li around, with a small fort called Licheng. Wang Yi said, "Licheng is small but defensible, and offers fish, lotus, and water chestnuts—we cannot let it go."

sentences.zh: 留偏將李直守寧晉，身率衆保瀝城，由是全活者衆。

translations.literal: He left the deputy general Li Zhi to hold Ningjin and personally led the multitude to defend Licheng; thereby many were wholly preserved.
translations.idiomatic: He left the deputy Li Zhi to hold Ningjin and led his men to Licheng, saving a great many lives.

sentences.zh: 歲乙亥，金將李伯祥據趙州，木華黎遣義擣其城。

translations.literal: In the yihai year the Jin general Li Boxiang held Zhao Prefecture; Muqali sent Yi to storm his city.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year, when the Jin general Li Boxiang held Zhao Prefecture, Muqali sent Wang Yi to assault the city.

sentences.zh: 會天大風雨，義帥壯士，挾長梯，疾趨，夜四鼓，四面齊登，殺守埤者。

translations.literal: A great wind and rain came; Yi led stalwart men carrying long ladders, rushed forward, and at the fourth watch of the night scaled the walls on all four sides and killed the wall defenders.
translations.idiomatic: A violent storm arose. Wang Yi led picked men with long ladders, rushed in at the fourth watch, and scaled the walls on all sides, killing the defenders on the ramparts.

sentences.zh: 城中亂，伯祥挺身走天壇寨，一州遂定。

translations.literal: The city fell into chaos; Boxiang fled alone to Tiantan Stockade, and the whole prefecture was settled.
translations.idiomatic: The city fell into disorder. Boxiang fled alone to Tiantan Stockade, and the prefecture was secured.

sentences.zh: 木華黎承制授義趙州太守、趙冀二州招撫使。

translations.literal: Muqali, acting by imperial commission, appointed Yi prefect of Zhao and pacification commissioner of Zhao and Ji.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali, exercising imperial authority, made Wang Yi prefect of Zhao and pacification commissioner for Zhao and Ji.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，大軍南取鉅鹿、洺州二城，還軍至唐陽西九門，遇金監軍納蘭率冀州節度使柴茂等，將兵萬餘北行。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year the great army south took the two cities of Julu and Ming Prefecture; returning, the army reached Jiumen west of Tangyang and encountered the Jin military supervisor Nalan leading Jizhou military commissioner Chai Mao and others with more than ten thousand troops marching north.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingchou year the main force took Julu and Mingzhou in the south. On the return march they reached Jiumen west of Tangyang and met the Jin military supervisor Nalan, with Jizhou commissioner Chai Mao and others, marching north with more than ten thousand men.

sentences.zh: 義伏兵桑林，先以百騎挑之，納蘭趨來迎戰，因稍却，誘之近桑林，伏起，金兵大亂，奔還，獲納蘭二弟及萬戶李虎。

translations.literal: Yi ambushed troops in the mulberry groves, first sent a hundred horsemen to challenge them; Nalan hurried to meet the fight, then slightly withdrew, luring them near the mulberry groves; the ambush rose and the Jin army was thrown into great disorder and fled back; Nalan's two younger brothers and chiliarch Li Hu were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi hid men in the mulberry groves and sent a hundred horsemen to provoke them. Nalan rushed to engage, then feigned retreat, drawing them toward the groves. The ambush sprang up, the Jin forces broke, and Nalan's two younger brothers and the chiliarch Li Hu were taken.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，拔束鹿，進攻深州，守帥以城降。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year he took Shulu and advanced to attack Shen Prefecture; the defending commander surrendered the city.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he captured Shulu and advanced on Shen Prefecture, whose commander surrendered.

sentences.zh: 順天都元帥張柔上其功，陞深州節度使。

translations.literal: Shuntian Grand Marshal Zhang Rou reported his merit, and he was promoted to military commissioner of Shen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Marshal Zhang Rou of Shuntian reported his achievements, and he was promoted to military commissioner of Shen.

sentences.zh: 深冀趙三州招撫使。

translations.literal: Pacification commissioner of Shen, Ji, and Zhao prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He became pacification commissioner for Shen, Ji, and Zhao.

sentences.zh: 金將武仙以兵四萬來攻束鹿，仙諭軍士曰：「束鹿兵少無糧，城無樓櫓，一日可拔也。」

translations.literal: The Jin general Wu Xian came with forty thousand troops to attack Shulu; Xian told his soldiers: "Shulu has few troops and no grain; the city has no towers or covered galleries—it can be taken in a day."
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wu Xian attacked Shulu with forty thousand men. He told his troops, "Shulu has few defenders and little grain, and no towers on the walls—it can be taken in a day."

sentences.zh: 盡銳來攻，義隨機應拒，積三十日不能下，大小數十戰皆捷。

translations.literal: He brought his full strength to the attack; Yi responded as circumstances required; for thirty days they could not take it, and in several dozen battles large and small he was victorious.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian attacked with his full force. Wang Yi met each move as it came. For thirty days the city held, and in dozens of engagements, large and small, he prevailed.

sentences.zh: 一夕，義召將佐曰：「今城守雖有餘，然外無援兵，糧食將盡，豈可坐而待斃。」

translations.literal: One night Yi summoned his officers and said: "Though we still have surplus for defense, we have no outside relief and our grain will soon be exhausted—how can we sit and await death?"
translations.idiomatic: One night Wang Yi told his officers, "We can still hold the walls, but there is no relief from outside and our grain is nearly gone. We cannot simply wait to be destroyed."

sentences.zh: 椎牛饗士，率精銳三千，銜枚夜出，直擣仙營。

translations.literal: He slaughtered oxen to feast the soldiers, led three thousand picked troops with gags in their mouths, and sallied by night straight at Xian's camp.
translations.idiomatic: He feasted his men on slaughtered cattle, then led three thousand picked troops with gags in their mouths in a night sortie straight at Wu Xian's camp.

sentences.zh: 仙軍亂，乘暗攻之，殺數千人。

translations.literal: Xian's army was thrown into disorder; taking advantage of the darkness they attacked and killed several thousand men.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian's army broke. In the darkness they struck and killed several thousand.

sentences.zh: 仙率餘衆遁還真定，悉獲其軍資器仗。

translations.literal: Xian led the remainder in flight back to Zhending and all their military supplies and weapons were captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian fled with the survivors to Zhending, and all their stores and arms were taken.

sentences.zh: 木華黎聞之，遣使送銀牌十，命義賜有功者。

translations.literal: When Muqali heard of it he sent an envoy with ten silver plaques and ordered Yi to award them to those who had merit.
translations.idiomatic: Muqali heard the news and sent ten silver plaques with orders for Wang Yi to reward the deserving.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，拔冀州，獲柴茂，械送軍前，木華黎、張柔復上其功，授龍虎衛上將軍、安武軍節度使，行深冀二州元帥府事，賜金虎符。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year he took Ji Prefecture, captured Chai Mao, sent him in fetters to headquarters; Muqali and Zhang Rou again reported his merit, and he was appointed General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard, military commissioner of the Anwu Army, acting marshal of the Shen and Ji prefectures, and granted a gold tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year he seized Ji Prefecture, captured Chai Mao, and sent him in bonds to headquarters. Muqali and Zhang Rou again reported his achievements. He was made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and military commissioner of the Anwu Army, with acting command of the Shen and Ji marshal's offices, and was granted a gold tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，仙復遣其將盧秀、李伯祥，率兵謀襲趙州，并取瀝城，率戰艦數百艘，沿江而下。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year Xian again sent his generals Lu Xiu and Li Boxiang with troops plotting to raid Zhao Prefecture and seize Licheng, leading several hundred warships down the river.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year Wu Xian again sent his generals Lu Xiu and Li Boxiang to strike at Zhao Prefecture and take Licheng, sailing several hundred warships downriver.

sentences.zh: 義具舟楫於紀家莊，截其下流，邀擊之，義士卒皆水鄉人，善水戰，回旋開闔，往來如風雨，船接，則躍登彼船，奮戈疾擊，敵莫能當，殺千餘人，擒秀。

translations.literal: Yi prepared boats at Jijiazhuang, intercepted them downstream, and attacked; Yi's soldiers were all men of the water country, skilled in naval combat; wheeling and opening and closing they moved like wind and rain; when the ships met they leaped aboard the enemy vessels and struck fiercely with spears—the enemy could not withstand them and more than a thousand were killed; Xiu was captured.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yi stationed boats at Jijiazhuang, blocked them downstream, and gave battle. His men were river folk, expert in water fighting; wheeling and darting like a storm, they leaped aboard enemy ships and struck with spears. The foe could not stand against them—over a thousand were killed and Lu Xiu taken.

sentences.zh: 伯祥退保瀝城，義引兵拔之，伯祥西走，二子死焉。

translations.literal: Boxiang withdrew to defend Licheng; Yi led troops and stormed it; Boxiang fled west and two of his sons died there.
translations.idiomatic: Boxiang retreated to Licheng. Wang Yi stormed the place; Boxiang fled west, and two of his sons died in the fighting.

sentences.zh: 邢州盜號趙大王，聚衆數千，據任縣固城水寨，真定史天澤集諸道兵攻之不能下。

translations.literal: A bandit of Xing Prefecture styled himself King Zhao, gathered several thousand men, and held the Gucheng water stockade in Ren County; Shitianze of Zhending assembled troops from every circuit to attack but could not take it.
translations.idiomatic: A Xingzhou outlaw called himself King Zhao, mustered several thousand men, and held the Gucheng water stockade in Ren County. Shi Tianze of Zhending gathered forces from every circuit but could not reduce it.

sentences.zh: 甲午，義引兵薄其城，一鼓下之，獲趙大王、侯縣令等數人殺之，餘黨悉平。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year Yi led troops to press the city; at one drum it fell; King Zhao, the magistrate of Hou County, and several others were captured and killed, and the remaining partisans were all pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year Wang Yi advanced on the stockade and took it at the first assault. King Zhao, the magistrate of Hou County, and several others were captured and executed, and the rest of the band was pacified.

sentences.zh: 義乃布教令，招集散亡，勸率種藝，深、冀之間，遂為樂土云。

translations.literal: Yi then promulgated teaching orders, summoned and settled the scattered and fugitive, and encouraged planting; between Shen and Ji the land became a happy country, it is said.
translations.idiomatic: He then issued orders of instruction, gathered the displaced, and urged farming. Between Shen and Ji the country became peaceful once more, so it is recorded.

sentences.zh: 王玉忱附

translations.literal: Wang Yu; Chen attached
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu (Chen attached)

sentences.zh: 王玉，趙州寧晉人。

translations.literal: Wang Yu was a native of Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu came from Ningjin in Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 長身駢脅多力，金季為萬戶，鎮趙州。

translations.literal: Tall in stature, with paired ribs and great strength, in the late Jin he was a chiliarch garrisoning Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was tall, broad-chested, and very strong. In the late Jin he was a chiliarch stationed at Zhao Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太師、國王木華黎下中原，玉率衆來附，領本部軍，從攻邢、洺、磁三州，濟南諸郡，號長漢萬戶。

translations.literal: When the Grand Tutor and King Muqali descended into the Central Plains, Yu led his multitude to submit, commanded his own army, followed in attacks on the three prefectures Xing, Ming, and Ci and the commanderies of Jinan, and was styled Chief of the Long Han Myriarchate.
translations.idiomatic: When the Grand Tutor and King Muqali entered the Central Plains, Wang Yu submitted with his troops, led his own command, and joined campaigns against Xing, Ming, and Ci and the Jinan region, taking the title Chief of the Long Han Myriarchate.

sentences.zh: 從攻澤、潞諸州，獨潞州堅壁不下，玉力戰，流矢中左目，竟拔其城。

translations.literal: He followed in attacks on Ze and Lu prefectures; Lu Prefecture alone held out behind strong walls; Yu fought fiercely, was struck in the left eye by a stray arrow, and in the end stormed the city.
translations.idiomatic: He campaigned against Ze and Lu. Lu alone held behind stout walls. Wang Yu fought hard, took an arrow in the left eye, and finally took the city.

sentences.zh: 又破平陽，下太原、汾、代等州。

translations.literal: He also stormed Pingyang and took Taiyuan, Fen, Dai, and other prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: He also captured Pingyang and took Taiyuan, Fen, Dai, and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 師還，署元帥府監軍，以趙州四十寨隸焉。

translations.literal: When the army returned he was appointed overseer of the marshal's headquarters, and the forty stockades of Zhao Prefecture were placed under him.
translations.idiomatic: On the army's return he was made overseer of the marshal's headquarters, with the forty stockades of Zhao placed under his command.

sentences.zh: 先是，金將武仙既降復叛，殺元帥史天倪。

translations.literal: Earlier the Jin general Wu Xian had submitted and then rebelled again, killing Marshal Shi Tianni.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier the Jin general Wu Xian had surrendered, then rebelled again and killed Marshal Shi Tianni.

sentences.zh: 宋將彭義斌在大名，陰與仙合，玉從笑乃帶、史天澤，攻敗武仙，生擒義斌，駐軍寧晉東里寨。

translations.literal: The Song general Peng Yibin was at Daming and secretly joined with Xian; Yu followed Xiao Naidai and Shi Tianze, defeated Wu Xian, captured Yibin alive, and encamped at Dongli Stockade in Ningjin.
translations.idiomatic: The Song general Peng Yibin was at Daming and colluded with Wu Xian. Wang Yu joined Xiao Naidai and Shi Tianze, defeated Wu Xian, captured Yibin alive, and camped at Dongli Stockade in Ningjin.

sentences.zh: 仙遣人齎誥命，誘玉妻，妻拒曰：「妾豈可使夫懷二心於國家耶！」

translations.literal: Xian sent a man bearing an edict of appointment to entice Yu's wife; the wife refused, saying: "How could I let my husband harbor a divided heart toward the state!"
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian sent a man with an edict of appointment to win over Wang Yu's wife. She refused: "How could I let my husband waver in loyalty to the state!"

sentences.zh: 仙圍之數匝，殺其子寧壽。

translations.literal: Xian besieged them for several circuits and killed their son Ningshou.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian besieged them for several rounds and killed their son Ningshou.

sentences.zh: 玉聞之，領數騎突其圍，斬獲數百人而還。

translations.literal: When Yu heard of it he led several horsemen and burst through the encirclement, killed and captured several hundred men, and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Hearing this, Wang Yu led a few horsemen through the siege, killed and captured several hundred, and returned.

sentences.zh: 仙遣人追之，不敢進，皆曰：「王將軍膽氣驍雄，我輩非敵也。」

translations.literal: Xian sent men to pursue him but dared not advance; all said: "General Wang's courage and spirit are fierce and heroic—we are no match for him."
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian sent pursuers but none dared close in. They all said, "General Wang is terrifyingly bold—we are no match for him."

sentences.zh: 仙乃盡發玉先世二十七冢，棄骸滿道。

translations.literal: Xian then exhumed all twenty-seven tombs of Yu's forebears and cast the bones along the road.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian then opened all twenty-seven ancestral tombs of Wang Yu's line and scattered the bones along the road.

sentences.zh: 玉從史天澤諸將，擊仙於趙州，仙糧絕，走雙門寨，圍之。

translations.literal: Yu followed Shi Tianze and the other generals and attacked Xian at Zhao Prefecture; Xian's grain was exhausted and he fled to Shuangmen Stockade, which was besieged.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu followed Shi Tianze and the other commanders against Wu Xian at Zhao. When Wu Xian's grain ran out he fled to Shuangmen Stockade and was besieged there.

sentences.zh: 會大風，仙獨脫走，斬其將四十三人，真定遂平。

translations.literal: A great wind arose and Xian alone escaped; forty-three of his generals were beheaded and Zhending was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: A fierce wind blew up and Wu Xian alone escaped. Forty-three of his generals were beheaded, and Zhending was pacified.

sentences.zh: 加定遠將軍，權真定五路萬戶，假趙州慶源軍節度副使。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Stabilizing-the-Distant General, acting myriarch of the five circuits of Zhending, and provisional vice military commissioner of the Qingyuan Army of Zhao Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Stabilizing-the-Distant General, made acting myriarch of Zhending's five circuits, and provisional vice commissioner of the Qingyuan Army at Zhao.

sentences.zh: 有民負西域賈人銀，倍其母，不能償，玉出銀五千兩代償之。

translations.literal: A commoner owed a Western Regions merchant silver at double the principal and could not repay; Yu produced five thousand taels of silver to repay on his behalf.
translations.idiomatic: A commoner owed a merchant from the Western Regions silver at double the principal and could not pay. Wang Yu paid five thousand taels of silver on his behalf.

sentences.zh: 又出家奴二百餘口為良民。

translations.literal: He also released more than two hundred household slaves as free commoners.
translations.idiomatic: He also freed more than two hundred household slaves as commoners.

sentences.zh: 中統元年二月卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the second month of the first year of Zhongtong he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the second month of the first Zhongtong year, at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子忱。

translations.literal: His son Chen.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Chen.

sentences.zh: 趙迪，真定藁城人也。

translations.literal: Zhao Di was a native of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Di came from Gaocheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，事母孝，多力善騎射。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he served his mother filially; he had great strength and was skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he was devoted to his mother, powerfully built, and expert in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 金末為義軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In the late Jin he was a chiliarch of the righteous army.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Jin period he was a chiliarch of the local militia.

sentences.zh: 郡將出六鈞強弩，立賞募能挽者，迪能之，即署真定尉，遷藁城尉，陞為丞。

translations.literal: The prefectural commander produced a six-jun strong crossbow and offered a reward for anyone who could draw it; Di could do so and was immediately appointed defender of Zhending, then defender of Gaocheng, and promoted to assistant magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: The prefect put up a six-jun crossbow and offered a prize to whoever could draw it. Di succeeded and was made defender of Zhending, then of Gaocheng, and later promoted to assistant magistrate.

sentences.zh: 太祖兵至藁城，迪率衆迎降。

translations.literal: When Taizu's army reached Gaocheng, Di led the multitude to welcome and submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan's army reached Gaocheng, Zhao Di led the people out to surrender.

sentences.zh: 歲壬午，改藁城為永安州，以迪同知節度使事。

translations.literal: In the renwu year Gaocheng was renamed Yong'an Prefecture and Di was made associate military commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year Gaocheng was renamed Yong'an Prefecture, and Di was appointed associate military commissioner.

sentences.zh: 嘗從帝西征，他將校豪橫俘掠，獨迪治軍嚴，所過無犯。

translations.literal: He once followed the emperor on the western campaign; other commanders were overbearing and seized captives, but Di alone kept his army strict and wherever they passed there was no violation.
translations.idiomatic: On a western campaign he marched with the emperor. Other officers looted freely, but Di kept his troops disciplined and allowed no harm where they passed.

sentences.zh: 先是，真定既破，迪亟入索藁城人在城中者，得男女千餘人，諸將欲分取之，迪曰：「是皆我所掠，當以歸我。」

translations.literal: Earlier, after Zhending had fallen, Di hurried in to demand the Gaocheng people who were in the city; he obtained more than a thousand men and women; the generals wished to divide and take them; Di said: "These are all people I captured—they ought to be returned to me."
translations.idiomatic: After Zhending fell, Di at once demanded the Gaocheng people held in the city and recovered more than a thousand men and women. When the other generals wanted to divide them as spoils, he said, "These are people I took—they should come back to me."

sentences.zh: 諸將許諾，迪乃召其人謂曰：「吾懼若屬為他將所得，則分奴之矣，故索以歸之我。

translations.literal: The generals agreed; Di then summoned the people and told them: "I feared that if you fell into other generals' hands you would be divided as slaves, so I demanded you be returned to me.
translations.idiomatic: They agreed. Zhao Di then told the people, "I was afraid that if other commanders got you, you would be enslaved and divided among them, so I claimed you for myself.

sentences.zh: 今縱汝往，宜各遂生產，為良民。」

translations.literal: Now I release you to go; you should each resume production and become good commoners."
translations.idiomatic: Now I set you free. Go home, resume your livelihoods, and live as honest subjects."

sentences.zh: 衆感泣而去。

translations.literal: The multitude departed weeping with gratitude.
translations.idiomatic: They left in tears of gratitude.

sentences.zh: 時兵荒之餘，骸骨蔽野，迪為大塚收瘞。

translations.literal: At that time, in the aftermath of war, bones covered the wilds; Di made a great mound and gathered them for burial.
translations.idiomatic: In the wasteland left by war, bones lay everywhere. He raised a great burial mound and interred them.

sentences.zh: 壬子歲卒，年七十。

translations.literal: In the renzi year he died, aged seventy.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the renzi year at the age of seventy.

sentences.zh: 子七人，椿齡，真定路轉運使。

translations.literal: He had seven sons; Chunling became transport commissioner of the Zhending circuit.
translations.idiomatic: He had seven sons; Chunling served as transport commissioner of the Zhending circuit.

sentences.zh: 邸順，保定行唐人，占籍於曲陽縣。

translations.literal: Di Shun was a native of Xingtang in Baoding, with household registration in Quyang County.
translations.idiomatic: Di Shun came from Xingtang in Baoding and was registered in Quyang County.

sentences.zh: 金末盜起，順會諸族，集鄉人豪壯數百人，與其弟常，築兩寨于石城、玄保，分據以守。

translations.literal: When bandits arose in the late Jin, Shun gathered the clans and assembled several hundred stalwart townsmen; with his younger brother Chang he built two stockades at Shicheng and Xuanbao and held them in divided defense.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Jin, when banditry spread, Shun rallied his kin and several hundred strong men of the district. With his brother Chang he built stockades at Shicheng and Xuanbao and held them in tandem.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，率衆來歸，太祖授行唐令。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year he led his multitude to submit; Taizu appointed him magistrate of Xingtang.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year he came over with his followers, and Genghis Khan made him magistrate of Xingtang.

sentences.zh: 丙子，真定饑，群盜據城叛，民皆穴地以避之，盜發地而噉其人，順擒數百人殺之。

translations.literal: In the bingzi year Zhending suffered famine; bandits seized the city in revolt; the people all burrowed underground to escape; the bandits dug them out and devoured them; Shun captured several hundred and killed them.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingzi year famine struck Zhending. Rebels held the city while people hid in underground shelters; the rebels dug them out and ate them. Shun seized several hundred bandits and executed them.

sentences.zh: 朝廷陞曲陽為恒州，以順為安撫使。

translations.literal: The court promoted Quyang to Heng Prefecture and made Shun pacification commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: The court elevated Quyang to Heng Prefecture and appointed Shun its pacification commissioner.

sentences.zh: 金將武仙據真定，帥衆來攻，順與戰，大敗之，賜金虎符，加鎮國上將軍、恒州等處都元帥。

translations.literal: The Jin general Wu Xian held Zhending and led troops to attack; Shun fought him and inflicted a great defeat; he was granted a gold tiger tally and advanced to General Who Secures the State and grand marshal of Heng Prefecture and other places.
translations.idiomatic: The Jin general Wu Xian held Zhending and attacked. Shun met him in battle and routed him. He received a gold tiger tally and was made General Who Secures the State and grand marshal of Heng and neighboring districts.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，武仙屯兵于黃、堯兩山，順及弟常又擊敗之。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year Wu Xian encamped his troops on Mount Huang and Mount Yao; Shun and his brother Chang again defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year Wu Xian camped on Mount Huang and Mount Yao. Shun and Chang defeated him again.

sentences.zh: 時西京郝道章，陰結武仙，抄掠州縣，順擒道章殺之，仙退真定以自保。

translations.literal: At that time Hao Daozhang of the Western Capital secretly joined Wu Xian and raided prefectures and districts; Shun captured Daozhang and killed him; Xian withdrew to Zhending to protect himself.
translations.idiomatic: Hao Daozhang of the Western Capital secretly allied with Wu Xian and raided the region. Shun captured and killed him, and Wu Xian fell back on Zhending.

sentences.zh: 順從木華黎攻之，敗之於王柳口，仙遂棄真定南走。

translations.literal: Shun followed Muqali in attacking him, defeated him at Wangliukou, and Xian then abandoned Zhending and fled south.
translations.idiomatic: Shun followed Muqali against him, defeated him at Wangliukou, and Wu Xian abandoned Zhending and fled south.

sentences.zh: 以功，賜順名察納合兒，陞驃騎衛上將軍，充山前都元帥；

translations.literal: For merit he was granted the name Chanaqer, promoted to General of the Swift-Cavalry Guard, and made grand marshal before the mountains;
translations.idiomatic: For his service he was given the name Chanaqer, promoted to General of the Swift-Cavalry Guard, and made grand marshal of the districts before the mountains;

sentences.zh: 弟常，賜名金那合兒。

translations.literal: his younger brother Chang was granted the name Jinnaghaer.
translations.idiomatic: his brother Chang received the name Jinnaghaer.

sentences.zh: 辛卯春，從太宗攻河南諸郡，招降民十餘萬，以順知中山府。

translations.literal: In the spring of the xinmao year he followed Taizong in attacking the prefectures of Henan, induced more than a hundred thousand people to submit, and Shun was made administrator of Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of xinmao he followed Ögedei Khan in the Henan campaign, brought over more than a hundred thousand people, and was put in charge of Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 己亥，佩金符，為行軍萬戶，管領諸路元差軍五千人。

translations.literal: In the jihai year he wore a gold tally, served as campaign myriarch, and commanded five thousand troops of the various circuits on imperial assignment.
translations.idiomatic: In the jihai year he was given a gold tally as campaign myriarch, commanding five thousand troops levied from the circuits.

sentences.zh: 從大軍破歸德府，留順戍之。

translations.literal: He followed the great army in storming Guide Prefecture and was left to garrison it.
translations.idiomatic: He joined the main force in taking Guide Prefecture and was left to garrison it.

sentences.zh: 丁未，駐師五河口，宋兵夜襲營，順掩殺其衆，生獲十五人。

translations.literal: In the dingwei year the army encamped at Wuhekou; Song troops raided the camp by night; Shun ambushed and killed their multitude and captured fifteen men alive.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingwei year, while the army was at Wuhekou, Song forces raided by night. Shun ambushed them, killed many, and took fifteen alive.

sentences.zh: 癸丑，攻漣水。

translations.literal: In the guichou year he attacked Lianshui.
translations.idiomatic: In the guichou year he assaulted Lianshui.

sentences.zh: 甲寅，舉部屬肖撤八、耨鄰之功以奏，上賜肖撤八、耨鄰金銀符，仍隸麾下。

translations.literal: In the jiayin year he reported the merit of his subordinates Xiao Sabah and Noulin to the throne; the emperor granted Xiao Sabah and Noulin gold and silver tallies, and they remained under his command.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiayin year he memorialized the achievements of his subordinates Xiao Sabah and Noulin. The emperor awarded them gold and silver tallies, and they remained under his command.

sentences.zh: 丙辰春，順卒，年七十四。

translations.literal: In the spring of the bingchen year Shun died, aged seventy-four.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of bingchen he died at seventy-four.

sentences.zh: 子浹，襲職。

translations.literal: His son Jia inherited the post.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jia succeeded to his office.

sentences.zh: 己未，從世祖渡江，圍鄂州，有戰功。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year he followed Shizu across the river and besieged E Prefecture, winning merit in battle.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiwei year he crossed the Yangtze with Kublai Khan and besieged Ezhou with distinction.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，世祖即位，浹以所部張宣等十二人奏聞于朝，遂以金銀符賜之。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong, when Shizu took the throne, Jia reported to the court twelve men of his command including Zhang Xuan, and they were thereupon granted gold and silver tallies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Zhongtong year, when Kublai ascended the throne, Jia presented twelve officers under his command, including Zhang Xuan, and they received gold and silver tallies.

sentences.zh: 三年，圍李璮，還守息州。

translations.literal: In the third year he besieged Li Tan and then returned to garrison Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he joined the siege of Li Tan, then returned to garrison Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 至元十一年，賜虎符，授金州招討副使，後又遷懷遠大將軍、金州萬戶。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year of Zhiyuan he was granted a tiger tally and appointed deputy pacification commissioner of Jin Prefecture; later he was transferred to Grand Far-Reaching General and myriarch of Jin Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 11 he received a tiger tally as deputy pacification commissioner of Jin Prefecture, and later became Grand Far-Reaching General and myriarch of Jin.

sentences.zh: 十三年，改襄陽管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was changed to myriarch commanding troops at Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he was reassigned as myriarch of the Xiangyang garrison.

sentences.zh: 三月，以樞密院奏，行淮西緫管萬戶府事，守廬州。

translations.literal: In the third month, on memorial of the Bureau of Military Affairs, he acted as overall myriarch of the Huaixi headquarters and garrisoned Luzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month, on petition from the Bureau of Military Affairs, he served as acting overall myriarch of the Huaixi command and garrisoned Luzhou.

sentences.zh: 十四年，移龍興，仍管領本翼軍人。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was transferred to Longxing, still commanding the troops of his wing.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was moved to Longxing while retaining command of his wing.

sentences.zh: 十五年，復為管軍萬戶，攻贛州崖石寨、太平岩賊有功。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he again became commanding myriarch and attacked the bandits of Yashizhai in Ganzhou and Taipingyan with merit.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he again became commanding myriarch and distinguished himself against bandits at Yashizhai in Ganzhou and at Taipingyan.

sentences.zh: 十七年，陞鎮國上將軍、都元帥，鎮龍興諸路，兼管本萬戶府事，賜銀印。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was promoted to General Who Secures the State and grand marshal, garrisoning the circuits of Longxing and concurrently administering his myriarchate; he was granted a silver seal.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he rose to General Who Secures the State and grand marshal of the Longxing region, with concurrent charge of his myriarchate, and received a silver seal.

sentences.zh: 吉、贛盜起，行省遷元帥府以鎮之。

translations.literal: When bandits arose in Ji and Gan, the branch secretariat moved the marshal's headquarters to suppress them.
translations.idiomatic: When banditry broke out in Ji and Gan, the regional office shifted the marshal's headquarters to suppress it.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，元帥府罷，復為萬戶。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year the marshal's headquarters was abolished and he again became a myriarch.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year the marshal's headquarters was dissolved and he again held the rank of myriarch.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，佩元降虎符，為歸德萬戶，鎮守吉安。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year he wore the tally for surrendered Yuan subjects, became myriarch of Guide, and garrisoned Ji'an.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year he bore the tally for surrendered subjects, became myriarch of Guide, and garrisoned Ji'an.

sentences.zh: 未幾，統領江西各萬戶，集兵七千戍廣東，凡二載。

translations.literal: Before long he commanded the various myriarchs of Jiangxi, gathered seven thousand troops to garrison Guangdong, for two years in all.
translations.idiomatic: Soon afterward he took command of the Jiangxi myriarchs, assembled seven thousand men to garrison Guangdong, and remained there two years.

sentences.zh: 大德三年卒，年七十七。

translations.literal: In the third year of Dade he died, aged seventy-seven.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third Dade year at seventy-seven.

sentences.zh: 贈輔國上將軍、北庭元帥府都元帥、護軍，追封高陽郡公，諡襄敏。

translations.literal: He was posthumously granted General Who Assists the State, Grand Marshal of the Beiting Marshalate, and Guardian of the Army; enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Xiangmin.
translations.idiomatic: Posthumously he was made General Who Assists the State, grand marshal of the Beiting headquarters, and Guardian of the Army, enfeoffed as Duke of Gaoyang with the posthumous title Xiangmin.

sentences.zh: 子榮仁，襲佩其虎符，為宣武將軍、歸德萬戶，鎮廣東惠州，感瘴疾，不任事。

translations.literal: His son Rongren inherited wearing his tiger tally, as Manifest Martial General and myriarch of Guide, garrisoning Huizhou in Guangdong; he suffered from miasma and could not perform his duties.
translations.idiomatic: His son Rongren inherited his tiger tally as Manifest Martial General and myriarch of Guide, stationed at Huizhou in Guangdong, but fell ill with miasma and could not serve.

sentences.zh: 子貫襲。

translations.literal: His son Guan inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His son Guan succeeded.

sentences.zh: 貫卒，子士忠襲。

translations.literal: When Guan died, his son Shizhong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Guan died, his son Shizhong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 士忠卒，子文襲。

translations.literal: When Shizhong died, his son Wen inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Shizhong died, his son Wen succeeded.

sentences.zh: 順族弟琮。

translations.literal: Shun's clansman Cong.
translations.idiomatic: A clansman of Shun's, Cong.

sentences.zh: 琮，太祖時從族兄行唐元帥常來降。

translations.literal: Cong, in Taizu's time, followed his cousin Chang, grand marshal of Xingtang, to submit.
translations.idiomatic: Cong came over in Genghis Khan's time with his cousin Chang, the Xingtang grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 歲乙酉，金降將武仙，復據真定叛，琮敗之于黃臺。

translations.literal: In the yiyou year the surrendered Jin general Wu Xian again held Zhending in rebellion; Cong defeated him at Huangtai.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiyou year the surrendered Jin general Wu Xian rebelled and held Zhending again. Cong defeated him at Huangtai.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，從元帥盞滅金于蔡，有功，真定五路萬戶選充緫管府推官。

translations.literal: In the guisi year he followed the marshal in destroying Jin at Cai and won merit; he was selected from the Zhending five-circuit myriarchs to serve as investigating officer of the overall headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year he followed the marshal in the final destruction of Jin at Caizhou and distinguished himself. He was chosen from the Zhending five-circuit myriarchs as investigating officer of the overall headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋奉旨，賜金符，授管軍緫押，管領七路兵馬，鎮徐州。

translations.literal: Soon he received an edict, was granted a gold tally, appointed overall commander of troops, and commanded military forces of seven circuits, garrisoning Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon an edict granted him a gold tally as overall troop commander over seven circuits, with his base at Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 宋兵入境，琮戰却之。

translations.literal: When Song troops crossed the border, Cong fought and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Song forces crossed the border, Cong fought them off.

sentences.zh: 己亥，從大將察罕攻滁州，力戰，流矢中臍，明年卒。

translations.literal: In the jihai year he followed the great general Chaghan in attacking Chuzhou, fought fiercely, was struck in the navel by a stray arrow, and died the following year.
translations.idiomatic: In the jihai year he joined the great general Chaghan in the assault on Chuzhou, fought hard, took an arrow in the belly, and died the next year.

sentences.zh: 子澤襲，移鎮潁州。

translations.literal: His son Ze inherited and was transferred to garrison Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ze succeeded and was transferred to garrison Ying Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 宋兵攻潁，澤戰敗之。

translations.literal: When Song troops attacked Ying, Ze fought and defeated them.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song attacked Ying, Ze defeated them.

sentences.zh: 至元四年，從元帥阿朮，克平塞寨及老山。

translations.literal: In the fourth year of Zhiyuan he followed Marshal Aju and captured Pingsai Stockade and Lao Yin Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 4 he followed Marshal Aju in taking Pingsai Stockade and Lao Yin Mountain.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從沙洋奪六艦，皆論功受賞有差。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the campaign at Shayang and seized six warships; in each case merit was assessed and rewards differed.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he fought at Shayang and captured six warships; rewards were apportioned according to merit.

sentences.zh: 十二年，授武德將軍、管軍緫管，從攻潭州及靜江，累官懷遠大將軍、管軍萬戶、郴州路緫管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was appointed Martial Virtue General and overall troop commander; he followed attacks on Tan Prefecture and Jingjiang, and in accumulated offices became Grand Far-Reaching General, commanding myriarch, and darughachi of Chenzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he became Martial Virtue General and overall commander, joined the assaults on Tanzhou and Jingjiang, and rose through successive posts to Grand Far-Reaching General, commanding myriarch, and darughachi of Chenzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，改授廬州蒙古漢軍萬戶，尋遷潁州翼，會徽州績溪縣盜起，澤討平之。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he was reassigned as myriarch of the Mongol and Han army at Luzhou; soon he was transferred to the Ying wing; when bandits arose in Jixi County of Huizhou circuit he pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he was made myriarch of the Mongol and Han forces at Luzhou, then moved to the Ying wing. When bandits rose in Jixi County in Huizhou, he suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 二十八年，移鎮杭州，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-eighth year he was transferred to garrison Hangzhou and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-eighth year he was posted to Hangzhou and died there.

sentences.zh: 子元謙，襲為潁州萬戶。

translations.literal: His son Yuanqian inherited as myriarch of Ying Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuanqian succeeded as myriarch of Ying.

sentences.zh: 元謙卒，子祺襲。

translations.literal: When Yuanqian died, his son Qi inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Yuanqian died, his son Qi succeeded.

sentences.zh: 祺卒，子忠襲。

translations.literal: When Qi died, his son Zhong inherited.
translations.idiomatic: When Qi died, his son Zhong succeeded.

sentences.zh: 王善子慶端附

translations.literal: Wang Shan; Ziqingduan attached
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan (Ziqingduan attached)

sentences.zh: 王善字子善，真定藁城人。

translations.literal: Wang Shan, courtesy name Zishan, was a native of Gaocheng in Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan, styled Zishan, came from Gaocheng in Zhending.

sentences.zh: 父增，監本縣酒務，以孝行稱。

translations.literal: His father Zeng supervised the county wine monopoly and was famed for filial conduct.
translations.idiomatic: His father Zeng supervised the county wine monopoly and was known for filial piety.

sentences.zh: 善資儀雄偉，其音若鐘，多智略，尤精騎射。

translations.literal: Shan had imposing stature and presence; his voice was like a bell; he had much strategy and was especially skilled in mounted archery.
translations.idiomatic: Shan was imposing in bearing; his voice rang like a bell. He was resourceful and especially skilled in mounted archery.

sentences.zh: 金貞祐播遷，田疇荒蕪，人無所得食，善求食以奉母。

translations.literal: When the Jin moved the capital in the Zhenyou era, fields lay waste and people had nothing to eat; Shan sought food to support his mother.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin court fled the capital in the Zhenyou era, farmland lay fallow and people starved. Shan scavenged food to feed his mother.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，群盜蜂起，衆推善為長。

translations.literal: In the yihai year bandits swarmed like bees; the multitude raised Shan as chief.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year bandits rose everywhere, and the people chose Wang Shan as their leader.

sentences.zh: 善約束有法，備禦有方，盜不能犯，擢本縣主簿。

translations.literal: Shan had rules of restraint and methods of defense; bandits could not harm them; he was promoted to chief clerk of the county.
translations.idiomatic: He imposed strict discipline and sound defenses, so bandits could not touch them, and he was promoted to chief clerk of the county.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，權中山府治中。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year he was made acting administrative vice-director of Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he served as acting administrative vice-director of Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 時武仙鎮真定，陰蓄異志，忌善威名，密令知府李濟、府判郭安圖之。

translations.literal: At that time Wu Xian held Zhending and secretly harbored divergent aims; jealous of Shan's renown, he secretly ordered the prefect Li Ji and the vice-prefect Guo An to plot against him.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian held Zhending and nursed treacherous designs. Envying Wang Shan's fame, he secretly ordered Prefect Li Ji and Vice-Prefect Guo An to plot his death.

sentences.zh: 己卯秋，濟、安張宴伏兵，召善計事。

translations.literal: In the autumn of the jimao year Ji and An spread a feast with hidden troops and summoned Shan to discuss affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the autumn of jimao, Ji and An set a feast with hidden soldiers and summoned Shan on pretense of business.

sentences.zh: 善覺，即還治衆，倉卒得八十人，慷慨與盟，人爭自奮，遂誅濟、安。

translations.literal: Shan perceived it, immediately returned to rally his followers, and in haste gathered eighty men; he swore a passionate oath with them and men vied to exert themselves; he then executed Ji and An.
translations.idiomatic: Shan sensed the trap, rallied his men, and mustered eighty followers in haste. They swore a fierce oath and charged; he killed Ji and An.

sentences.zh: 乃諭其黨曰：「造釁者，李、郭耳，餘無所問。」

translations.literal: He then instructed his faction: "Those who made trouble were Li and Guo alone; the rest are not questioned."
translations.idiomatic: He told his men, "Only Li and Guo stirred this trouble. No one else will be punished."

sentences.zh: 善夜卧北城上，戒麾下曰：「勿以我累汝家，當取吾首獻帥府。」

translations.literal: Shan slept by night on the north city wall and warned his subordinates: "Do not let me implicate your households—you should take my head and present it to the marshal's headquarters."
translations.idiomatic: That night he slept on the north wall and told his followers, "Do not let me ruin your families—if need be, take my head to the marshal's headquarters."

sentences.zh: 衆曰：「公何為出此言，我輩惟有效死而已。」

translations.literal: All said: "Why does my lord speak thus? We can only devote our lives to death."
translations.idiomatic: They replied, "Why speak so, my lord? We will follow you to the death."

sentences.zh: 遂率衆來歸，授金符，同知中山府事。

translations.literal: Thereupon he led the multitude to submit; he was granted a gold tally and made associate administrator of Zhongshan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Then he led his men to submit. He received a gold tally and was made associate administrator of Zhongshan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 是年冬，以兵三百攻武仙，仙遣將率精銳二千拒戰，善擒斬之。

translations.literal: That winter he attacked Wu Xian with three hundred troops; Xian sent a general leading two thousand picked troops to resist; Shan captured and beheaded him.
translations.idiomatic: That winter he attacked Wu Xian with three hundred men. Wu Xian sent a general with two thousand elite troops; Shan captured and beheaded him.

sentences.zh: 仙走獲鹿，委其佐段琛城守，復戰拔之，入據其城，軍勢大振，自中山以南，降州郡四十二。

translations.literal: Xian fled to Hulu, left his aide Duan Chen to hold the city, fought again and stormed it, entered and occupied the city; his military power greatly flourished; from Zhongshan southward forty-two prefectures and districts submitted.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian fled to Hulu and left his aide Duan Chen to hold the city. Shan stormed it, occupied it, and his power swelled. Forty-two prefectures south of Zhongshan submitted.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，遷中山真定等路招討使，尋加右副元帥、驃騎大將軍，屯藁城。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year he was transferred to pacification commissioner of Zhongshan, Zhending, and other circuits; soon he was added as right vice marshal and Grand General of the Swift Cavalry, encamped at Gaocheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year he became pacification commissioner for Zhongshan, Zhending, and neighboring circuits, then right vice marshal and Grand General of the Swift Cavalry, with his camp at Gaocheng.

sentences.zh: 壬午，陞藁城為匡國軍，以善行帥府事。

translations.literal: In the renwu year Gaocheng was elevated to the Kuangguo Army and Shan administered the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year Gaocheng was raised to the Kuangguo Army, and Shan headed the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 癸未，進金吾衛大將軍、左副元帥。

translations.literal: In the guiwei year he was advanced to Grand General of the Golden Spear Guard and left vice marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiwei year he was promoted to Grand General of the Golden Spear Guard and left vice marshal.

sentences.zh: 仙窮迫請降，詔命復舊鎮。

translations.literal: Xian, driven to extremity, requested surrender; an edict ordered his former post restored.
translations.idiomatic: Cornered, Wu Xian asked to surrender, and an edict restored his former command.

sentences.zh: 善奏：「仙狼子野心，終必反覆，請修城隍備之。」

translations.literal: Shan memorialized: "Xian has the heart of a wolf cub—he will ultimately turn treacherous; I request that city walls and defenses be repaired."
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shan memorialized, "Wu Xian is treacherous by nature and will rebel again. Please strengthen the walls and prepare defenses."

sentences.zh: 未幾，仙果叛，率衆來攻，火及西門，善出戰，却之。

translations.literal: Before long Xian indeed rebelled, led troops to attack, and fire reached the west gate; Shan went out to fight and repelled them.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Wu Xian rebelled and attacked. Fire reached the west gate, but Shan sallied and drove him off.

sentences.zh: 仙使其部下宋元，俘老幼四千人南奔，善追奪之，俾復故業。

translations.literal: Xian had his subordinate Song Yuan seize four thousand old and young and flee south; Shan pursued, recovered them, and restored them to their former livelihoods.
translations.idiomatic: Wu Xian's officer Song Yuan seized four thousand old and young and fled south. Shan overtook him, recovered the people, and sent them home.

sentences.zh: 仙自是不敢復入真定，其部曲多來降。

translations.literal: Xian then did not dare enter Zhending again; many of his followers came to submit.
translations.idiomatic: After that Wu Xian dared not enter Zhending again, and many of his troops came over.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，以功賜金虎符，仍行帥府事。

translations.literal: In the bingxu year, for merit he was granted a gold tiger tally and still administered the marshal's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingxu year he received a gold tiger tally for his service and continued to head the marshal's headquarters.

sentences.zh: 壬辰，從征河南，至鄭州。

translations.literal: In the renchen year he followed the campaign in Henan as far as Zheng Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the renchen year he joined the Henan campaign as far as Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 州將馬伯堅素聞善名，登陴大呼曰：「藁城王元帥在軍中否？

translations.literal: The prefect Ma Bojian had long heard of Shan's name; he mounted the walls and shouted loudly: "Is the Gaocheng Wang Marshal in the army?
translations.idiomatic: The prefect Ma Bojian had long heard of Wang Shan. He mounted the wall and shouted, "Is Marshal Wang of Gaocheng in the camp?

sentences.zh: 願以城降之。」

translations.literal: I wish to surrender the city to him."
translations.idiomatic: I wish to surrender the city to him."

sentences.zh: 善直前，免冑與語，伯堅果率衆出降。

translations.literal: Shan went straight forward, removed his helmet and spoke with him; Bojian indeed led the multitude out to surrender.
translations.idiomatic: Shan went forward bareheaded and spoke with him. Bojian then led the people out in surrender.

sentences.zh: 善令軍中秋毫無犯，民皆按堵，願從善北渡者以萬計，授之土田，以安集之。

translations.literal: Shan ordered the army that not the slightest thing be violated; the people all remained secure in their homes; those who wished to follow Shan north across the river numbered in the tens of thousands; he granted them land to settle and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: He forbade the slightest harm to the people, who remained secure. Tens of thousands chose to follow him north; he allotted them farmland and settled them.

sentences.zh: 丙申，兼河北西路兵馬副都緫管。

translations.literal: In the bingshen year he was concurrently deputy overall commander of army and horse forces of the Hebei West Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingshen year he was also made deputy overall commander of the Hebei West Circuit.

sentences.zh: 辛丑，授知中山府事，屬縣新樂，地居衝要，迎送供給，倍於他縣，皆取於民。

translations.literal: In the xinchou year he was appointed administrator of Zhongshan Prefecture; the subordinate county Xinle lay on a vital route; reception and supply obligations were double those of other counties, all taken from the people.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinchou year he became administrator of Zhongshan Prefecture. The subordinate county Xinle lay on a main thoroughfare, and its hospitality levies were twice those of other counties, all exacted from the people.

sentences.zh: 善均其勞逸，所徵或未給，輒出家貲代輸，民德之。

translations.literal: Shan equalized their labor and rest; when what was levied was not yet delivered he would bring out his household wealth to pay on their behalf; the people were grateful to him.
translations.idiomatic: He balanced their burdens of labor and rest. When levies went unpaid he paid from his own estate, and the people blessed him for it.

sentences.zh: 又放家僮五百人為民，咸懷其恩。

translations.literal: He also released five hundred household servants as commoners; all cherished his kindness.
translations.idiomatic: He also freed five hundred household slaves as commoners, and all remembered his kindness.

sentences.zh: 癸卯卒，年六十一。

translations.literal: In the guimao year he died, aged sixty-one.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the guimao year at sixty-one.

sentences.zh: 皇慶元年，贈銀青榮祿大夫、司徒，追封冀國公，諡武靖。

translations.literal: In the first year of Huangqing he was posthumously granted Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with the posthumous title Wujing.
translations.idiomatic: In Huangqing 1 he was posthumously made Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal and Grand Tutor, enfeoffed as Duke of Ji with the posthumous title Wujing.

sentences.zh: 子慶淵，為行軍千戶，征淮南死；

translations.literal: His son Qingyuan served as campaign chiliarch, died on the Huainan campaign;
translations.idiomatic: His son Qingyuan was a campaign chiliarch and died on the Huainan campaign;

sentences.zh: 次慶端。

translations.literal: the next was Qingduan.
translations.idiomatic: the next son was Qingduan.

sentences.zh: 慶端字正甫，初為郡筦庫，進水軍提領，訓練士卒，常如臨敵。

translations.literal: Qingduan, courtesy name Zhengfu, at first was county warehouse clerk, advanced to naval commander, trained soldiers always as if facing the enemy.
translations.idiomatic: Qingduan, styled Zhengfu, began as county warehouse clerk, rose to naval commander, and drilled his troops as if always in battle.

sentences.zh: 敗李璮於老僧口，以功佩金符，為千戶。

translations.literal: He defeated Li Tan at Laosengkou; for merit he wore a gold tally and became a chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Li Tan at Laosengkou, received a gold tally for his service, and became a chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 監築大都城。

translations.literal: He oversaw construction of the great capital city.
translations.idiomatic: He supervised construction of Dadu.

sentences.zh: 移戍清口，宋兵來攻，守將戰死，城欲陷，慶端拔刀誓衆，裹創力戰，城得以全。

translations.literal: Transferred to garrison Qingkou, Song troops came to attack; the defending commander died in battle and the city was about to fall; Qingduan drew his sword and swore before the multitude, fought fiercely though wounded, and the city was preserved.
translations.idiomatic: Posted to Qingkou, he faced a Song assault after the garrison commander fell. As the city neared collapse he drew his sword, rallied the men, fought on despite wounds, and saved the city.

sentences.zh: 群盜四起，復擊走之。

translations.literal: Bandits rose everywhere; he again attacked and drove them off.
translations.idiomatic: When bandits rose in force he drove them off again.

sentences.zh: 進武節將軍、管軍緫管，領左右中衛兵。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Martial Integrity General and overall troop commander, commanding the left, right, and central guards.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Martial Integrity General and overall commander of the left, right, and central guards.

sentences.zh: 從世祖北征，還，遷右衛親軍副都指揮使，進侍衛軍都指揮使，建威武營，以處衛兵，經畫田廬，使各安業。

translations.literal: He followed Shizu on the northern campaign; on return he was transferred to deputy commander of the Right Guard, advanced to commander of the Palace Guard, built the Majestic Martial Camp to house guard troops, and planned fields and lodges so each could settle to his livelihood.
translations.idiomatic: He joined Kublai's northern campaign. On his return he became deputy commander of the Right Guard, then commander of the Palace Guard. He built the Majestic Martial Camp for the guards, laid out farms and quarters, and settled the men in livelihood.

sentences.zh: 別立神鋒軍，親教以蹶張弩技，作整暇堂、犀利局。

translations.literal: He separately established the Divine Vanguard Army and personally taught them crossbow-drawing technique, and built the Leisure Hall and the Sharp Office.
translations.idiomatic: He formed a separate Divine Vanguard Army, taught them crossbow technique himself, and built the Leisure Hall and Sharp Office.

sentences.zh: 浚渠構室，如治家事。

translations.literal: He dredged canals and built quarters as if managing his own household.
translations.idiomatic: He dredged canals and built quarters with the care of a household head.

sentences.zh: 至元十九年，改詹事丞，時有司欲就威武貸粟數萬石，濟饑民。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year of Zhiyuan he was changed to Vice-Director of the Household of the Heir Apparent; at that time the authorities wished to borrow several tens of thousands of piculs of grain from the Majestic Martial Camp to relieve starving people.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 19 he became vice-director of the heir apparent's household. The authorities wanted to borrow tens of thousands of piculs of grain from the Majestic Martial Camp to feed the hungry.

sentences.zh: 裕宗在東宮，以問慶端，慶端對曰：「兵民等耳，何間焉！」

translations.literal: The Heir Apparent was in the Eastern Palace and asked Qingduan; Qingduan replied: "Soldiers and commoners are equal—what distinction is there!"
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Zhenjin in the Eastern Palace asked his view. Qingduan answered, "Soldiers and civilians are the same—why make a distinction?"

sentences.zh: 即命與之。

translations.literal: He was immediately ordered to give it.
translations.idiomatic: The prince at once ordered the grain released.

sentences.zh: 帝嘗遣近侍夜出伺察，為邏卒所執，近侍以實告，卒曰：「軍中惟知將軍令，不知其他。」

translations.literal: The emperor once sent close attendants out by night to observe; they were seized by patrol soldiers; the attendants told the truth; the soldiers said: "In the army we know only the general's orders, not anything else."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor once sent close attendants out at night on inspection. Patrols seized them. When the attendants explained, the soldiers said, "In this army we know only the general's orders."

sentences.zh: 近侍以聞，帝賞以黑貂裘。

translations.literal: The attendants reported this; the emperor rewarded him with a black sable coat.
translations.idiomatic: The attendants reported this, and the emperor rewarded Qingduan with a black sable coat.

sentences.zh: 及親征乃顏，命慶端以所部從，時年六十餘，與士卒同甘苦，晝則擐甲執兵迎敵，夜卧不解衣，暇則俾士卒為軍市，自相懋遷。

translations.literal: When he personally campaigned against Nayan he ordered Qingduan to follow with his command; he was then over sixty and shared hardship with the soldiers; by day he donned armor and took weapons to meet the enemy; by night he slept without removing his clothes; in leisure he had the soldiers hold army markets among themselves for mutual trade.
translations.idiomatic: On the campaign against Nayan he took Qingduan and his troops. Though over sixty, he shared the men's hardships, fought armored by day, slept in armor by night, and in quiet moments let the soldiers trade in camp markets.

sentences.zh: 征東之功，慶端贊畫居多。

translations.literal: In the merit of the eastern campaign Qingduan's planning contribution was greatest.
translations.idiomatic: In the eastern campaign his planning contribution was among the greatest.

sentences.zh: 杜豐字唐臣，汾州西河人。

translations.literal: Du Feng, courtesy name Tangchen, was a native of Xihe in Fen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Du Feng, styled Tangchen, came from Xihe in Fen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父珪，以積德好施，鄉稱善人。

translations.literal: His father Gui was called a good man in the district for accumulated virtue and generous giving.
translations.idiomatic: His father Gui was known in the district for virtue and charity.

sentences.zh: 豐少有大志，倜儻不群，通兵法。

translations.literal: Feng in youth had great ambition, was unconventional and stood apart, and mastered military strategy.
translations.idiomatic: In youth Du Feng was ambitious, unconventional, and versed in military strategy.

sentences.zh: 仕金，為平遙義軍謀克，佩銀符。

translations.literal: He served the Jin as a Jurchen commander of the Pingyao righteous army and wore a silver tally.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin he was a Jurchen commander of the Pingyao militia and bore a silver tally.

sentences.zh: 太祖取太原，豐率所部來降。

translations.literal: When Taizu took Taiyuan, Feng led his command to submit.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan took Taiyuan, Du Feng surrendered with his command.

sentences.zh: 皇舅按赤那延授兵馬都提控。

translations.literal: The imperial maternal uncle Bo'orchu appointed him overall controller of army and horse.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial uncle Bo'orchu made him overall controller of army and horse.

sentences.zh: 從國王按察兒攻平陽，先登。

translations.literal: He followed King Chaghan in attacking Pingyang and was first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He followed King Chaghan in the assault on Pingyang and was first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 克絳州、解州諸堡，招集流民三萬餘家。

translations.literal: He stormed Jiang Prefecture, Jie Prefecture, and other stockades, and gathered more than thirty thousand refugee households.
translations.idiomatic: He took Jiangzhou, Jiezhou, and other strongpoints and gathered more than thirty thousand refugee households.

sentences.zh: 以功賜金虎符，陞征行元帥左監軍。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted a gold tiger tally and promoted to left overseer of the campaign grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: For his service he received a gold tiger tally and was made left overseer of the campaign grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 金人南遁，遂以豐守河北。

translations.literal: The Jin people fled south, and Feng was then made to guard Hebei.
translations.idiomatic: When the Jin court fled south, he was left to guard Hebei.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，上黨公張開以萬衆寇汾州，豐率精騎五千敗之。

translations.literal: In the gengchen year the Duke of Shangdang Zhang Kai came with ten thousand men to invade Fen Prefecture; Feng led five thousand picked horsemen and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengchen year Zhang Kai, Duke of Shangdang, invaded Fen with ten thousand men. Du Feng led five thousand picked horsemen and routed him.

sentences.zh: 從國王阿察兒，下懷孟，破溫谷、木澗等寨，輒先登。

translations.literal: He followed King Achar in taking Huai and Meng, storming Wengu, Mujian, and other stockades, always first to scale the walls.
translations.idiomatic: He followed King Achar in taking Huai and Meng and storming Wengu, Mujian, and other stockades, always first over the wall.

sentences.zh: 攻洪洞西山，斬首六百餘級。

translations.literal: Attacking Hongdong West Mountain he beheaded more than six hundred.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongdong West Mountain he took more than six hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 攻松平山，破之，賊墮崖死以萬計，獲生口甚衆。

translations.literal: He attacked Songping Mountain, broke it, and bandits who fell from the cliffs died by the tens of thousands; captives taken alive were very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: He stormed Songping Mountain. Many rebels fell from the cliffs to their deaths, and he took a great many prisoners.

sentences.zh: 金將武仙等，往來鈔掠平陽、太原間，行路梗塞。

translations.literal: The Jin generals Wu Xian and others came and went raiding between Pingyang and Taiyuan, and travel on the roads was blocked.
translations.idiomatic: Jin generals including Wu Xian raided back and forth between Pingyang and Taiyuan, choking the roads.

sentences.zh: 壬午，授豐龍虎衛上將軍、河東南北路兵馬都元帥，便宜行事。

translations.literal: In the renwu year Feng was appointed General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and grand marshal of the north and south routes of the Hedong army and horse, with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year he was made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and grand marshal of the north and south Hedong routes, with discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 遂破玉女、割渠等寨，俘獲千餘人。

translations.literal: He then stormed the stockades of Yunu, Gequ, and others, capturing more than a thousand.
translations.idiomatic: He then took the stockades of Yunu, Gequ, and others, capturing more than a thousand.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，從按赤那延攻益都，金守將突圍出，豐戰扼之，斬首千級，捕虜二十人，益都下，遂略地登、萊，降島民萬餘。

translations.literal: In the bingxu year he followed Bo'orchu in attacking Yidu; the Jin defending commander broke out; Feng fought to block him, beheaded a thousand, captured twenty, Yidu fell, and he then swept Deng and Lai, inducing more than ten thousand island people to submit.
