translations.idiomatic: In the bingxu year he followed Bo'orchu against Yidu. The Jin commander broke out; Du Feng blocked him, took a thousand heads and twenty captives, and Yidu fell. He then swept Deng and Lai and brought over ten thousand islanders.

sentences.zh: 己丑，以本部取沁州，由是銅鞮、武鄉、襄垣、綿上、沁源諸縣皆下。

translations.literal: In the jichou year with his own command he took Qin Prefecture, and thereby Tongdi, Wuxiang, Xiangyuan, Mianshang, Qinyuan, and other counties all fell.
translations.idiomatic: In the jichou year he took Qin Prefecture with his own troops, and with it Tongdi, Wuxiang, Xiangyuan, Mianshang, Qinyuan, and neighboring counties.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，命豐撫定平陽、太原、真定及遼、沁未降山寨，皆平之。

translations.literal: In the xinmao year he was ordered to pacify Pingyang, Taiyuan, Zhending, and the stockades of Liao and Qin not yet submitted—all were pacified.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinmao year he was ordered to pacify Pingyang, Taiyuan, Zhending, and the remaining stockades of Liao and Qin; all submitted.

sentences.zh: 乙未，陞沁州長官，長官者，國初高爵也。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year he was promoted to chief of Qin Prefecture; chief at that time was a high title in the founding of the state.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year he was promoted to chief of Qin Prefecture—at the founding of the dynasty, chief was a high rank.

sentences.zh: 在沁十餘年，寬徭薄賦，勸課農桑，民以富足。

translations.literal: For more than ten years in Qin he lightened corvée and taxes, encouraged farming and sericulture, and the people grew wealthy.
translations.idiomatic: For more than ten years in Qin he eased levies, encouraged farming and silkworms, and the people prospered.

sentences.zh: 丁未，請老。

translations.literal: In the dingwei year he requested retirement.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingwei year he asked to retire.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，疾卒于家，年六十有七。

translations.literal: In the bingchen year he died of illness at home, aged sixty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the bingchen year he died at home of illness, aged sixty-seven.

sentences.zh: 沁人立祠，歲時祀焉。

translations.literal: The people of Qin erected a shrine and sacrificed to him at the seasons.
translations.idiomatic: The people of Qin built him a shrine and offered seasonal sacrifice.

sentences.zh: 子三人：思明，思忠，思敬。

translations.literal: He had three sons: Siming, Sizhong, and Sijing.
translations.idiomatic: He had three sons: Siming, Sizhong, and Sijing.

sentences.zh: 思敬事世祖潛邸，由平陽路同知累遷治書侍御史。

translations.literal: Sijing served the heir apparent's residence when Shizu was still a prince; from associate administrator of the Pingyang circuit he rose in accumulated offices to investigating censor.
translations.idiomatic: Sijing served Kublai in his princely residence and rose from associate administrator of the Pingyang circuit to investigating censor.

sentences.zh: 阿合馬敗，臺臣皆罷去，思敬以帝所眷知，獨留。

translations.literal: When Ahmad fell, the censorate officials were all dismissed; Sijing alone remained because the emperor favored his knowledge.
translations.idiomatic: When Ahmad fell, the censorate was purged, but Sijing alone remained because the emperor valued his judgment.

sentences.zh: 出為安西路緫管，僉陝西行省事，歷汴梁緫管，再入中臺為侍御史。

translations.literal: He went out as overall administrator of the Anxi circuit, joined the Shaanxi branch secretariat, served as overall administrator of Bianliang, and again entered the central censorate as attendant censor.
translations.idiomatic: He served as overall administrator of Anxi, joined the Shaanxi secretariat, governed Bianliang, and returned to the central censorate as attendant censor.

sentences.zh: 時桑哥以罪誅，風紀為之振肅。

translations.literal: At that time Sangge had been executed for crime and discipline was thereby restored.
translations.idiomatic: After Sangge was executed for his crimes, official discipline revived.

sentences.zh: 未幾，拜參知政事，改四川行省左丞，不赴，陞中書左丞。

translations.literal: Before long he was appointed vice director of the Secretariat, changed to left cheng of the Sichuan branch secretariat but did not go, and was advanced to left cheng of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became vice director of the Secretariat, was named left cheng of Sichuan but declined, and was promoted to left cheng of the central Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 致仕，年八十六卒，諡文定。

translations.literal: He retired from office and died aged eighty-six; posthumous title Wending.
translations.idiomatic: He retired and died at eighty-six with the posthumous title Wending.

sentences.zh: 石抹孛迭兒

translations.literal: Shimo Bedieer
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Bedieer

sentences.zh: 石抹孛迭兒，契丹人。

translations.literal: Shimo Bedieer was a Khitan.
translations.idiomatic: Shimo Bedieer was a Khitan.

sentences.zh: 父桃葉兒，徙霸州。

translations.literal: His father Taoyeer was moved to Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: His father Taoyeer was relocated to Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 孛迭兒仕金，為霸州平曲水寨管民官。

translations.literal: Bedieer served the Jin as the official managing the people of the Pingqu Water Stockade in Bazhou.
translations.idiomatic: Bedieer served the Jin as civil administrator of the Pingqu water stockade in Bazhou.

sentences.zh: 太師、國王木華黎率師至霸州，孛迭兒迎降，木華黎察其智勇，奇之，擢為千戶。

translations.literal: When the Grand Tutor and King Muqali led troops to Bazhou, Bedieer came out to welcome and submit; Muqali observed his wisdom and courage, marveled at him, and promoted him to chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: When Muqali reached Bazhou, Bedieer surrendered. Muqali admired his intelligence and courage and made him a chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，從木華黎覲太祖於雄州，佩以銀符，充漢軍都統。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year he followed Muqali to have audience with Taizu at Xiong Prefecture, was granted a silver tally, and served as overall commander of Han troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year he followed Muqali to audience with Genghis Khan at Xiongzhou, received a silver tally, and became overall commander of Han forces.

sentences.zh: 帝次牛闌山，欲盡戮漢軍，木華黎以孛迭兒可用，奏釋之，因請隸麾下，從平高州。

translations.literal: The emperor halted at Niulanshan and wished to slaughter all Han troops; Muqali because Bedieer was usable memorialized to release them, and thereupon requested him under his command; he followed in pacifying Gaozhou.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor camped at Niulanshan and meant to slaughter the Han troops. Muqali pleaded that Bedieer was useful, secured their release, took him under command, and pacified Gaozhou.

sentences.zh: 乙亥，授左監軍，佩金符，與北京都元帥吾也兒，分領錦州紅羅山、北京東路漢軍二萬。

translations.literal: In the yihai year he was appointed left overseer, granted a gold tally, and with the Beiping Grand Marshal Uyar jointly commanded twenty thousand Han troops of the Jinzhou Hongluo Mountain and Beiping East Route.
translations.idiomatic: In the yihai year he became left overseer with a gold tally and, with Beiping Grand Marshal Uyar, commanded twenty thousand Han troops of Jinzhou's Hongluo Mountain and the Beiping eastern route.

sentences.zh: 又從奪忽闌闍里必徇地山東、大名。

translations.literal: He again followed Doqolqu in securing the lands of Shandong and Daming.
translations.idiomatic: He again followed Doqolqu in securing Shandong and Daming.

sentences.zh: 比至洺州，城守甚堅，師不得進，孛迭兒不避矢石，率衆先登，遂拔之。

translations.literal: When they reached Ming Prefecture the defense was very strong and the army could not advance; Bedieer did not avoid arrows and stones, led the multitude first to scale the walls, and in the end stormed it.
translations.idiomatic: At Mingzhou the defense was fierce and the army stalled. Bedieer, heedless of missiles, led his men first over the wall and took the city.

sentences.zh: 丁丑，從平益都、沂、密、萊、淄。

translations.literal: In the dingchou year he followed in pacifying Yidu, Yi, Mi, Lai, and Zi.
translations.idiomatic: In the dingchou year he helped pacify Yidu, Yi, Mi, Lai, and Zi.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，從定太原、忻、代、平陽、吉、隰、岢嵐、汾、石、絳州、河中、潞、澤、遼、沁。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year he followed in pacifying Taiyuan, Xin, Dai, Pingyang, Ji, Xi, Kelan, Fen, Shi, Jiang, Hezhong, Lu, Ze, Liao, and Qin.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he joined the pacification of Taiyuan, Xin, Dai, Pingyang, Ji, Xi, Kelan, Fen, Shi, Jiang, Hezhong, Lu, Ze, Liao, and Qin.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，木華黎承制陞孛迭兒為龍虎衛上將軍、霸州等路元帥，佩金虎符，以黑軍鎮守固安水寨。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year Muqali, acting by imperial commission, promoted Bedieer to General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and marshal of Bazhou and other circuits, granted a gold tiger tally, and with the Black Army garrisoned the Gu'an water stockade.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year Muqali, by imperial commission, made him General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and marshal of Bazhou and neighboring circuits, gave him a gold tiger tally, and stationed the Black Army at the Gu'an water stockade.

sentences.zh: 既至，令兵士屯田，且耕且戰，披荊棘，立廬舍，數年之間，城市悉完，為燕京外蔽。

translations.literal: Once there he ordered soldiers to farm the fields, fighting while they plowed; they cleared brambles and built lodges; within several years the city was complete and became an outer shield for Yanjing.
translations.idiomatic: There he had his men farm while they fought, cleared brush, and built quarters. Within a few years the settlement was complete and became an outer defense for Yanjing.

sentences.zh: 庚寅，朝太宗于行在所，賜金符。

translations.literal: In the gengyin year he had audience with Taizong at the mobile court and was granted a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the gengyin year he had audience with Ögedei Khan at the mobile court and received a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 辛卯，從國王塔思征河南。

translations.literal: In the xinmao year he followed King Tasi in the Henan campaign.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinmao year he followed King Tasi in the Henan campaign.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，從討萬奴於遼東，平之。

translations.literal: In the guisi year he followed in suppressing Wannu in Liaodong and pacified him.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year he joined the suppression of Wannu in Liaodong and pacified him.

sentences.zh: 孛迭兒始從征伐，及後為將，大小百戰，所至有功，年七十，以疾卒于官。

translations.literal: Bedieer at first followed campaigns; afterward as a general in large and small battles numbering a hundred, wherever he went he had merit; aged seventy he died of illness in office.
translations.idiomatic: From campaigns in his youth to command in later years, he fought a hundred engagements with merit each time. He died in office of illness at seventy.

sentences.zh: 子糾查剌、查茶剌。

translations.literal: His sons were Jiuchala and Chachala.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Jiuchala and Chachala.

sentences.zh: 賈塔剌渾

translations.literal: Jia Talahun
translations.idiomatic: Jia Talahun

sentences.zh: 賈塔剌渾，冀州人。

translations.literal: Jia Talahun was a native of Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Jia Talahun came from Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖用兵中原，募能用砲者籍為兵，授塔剌渾四路緫押，佩金符以將之。

translations.literal: When Taizu used troops in the Central Plains he recruited those who could use artillery and registered them as soldiers; Talahun was appointed overall commander of four routes, granted a gold tally to lead them.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan campaigned in the Central Plains he enrolled men skilled with artillery. Talahun was made overall commander of four routes with a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 及攻益都，下之，加龍虎衛上將軍、行元帥左監軍，便宜行事。

translations.literal: When they attacked Yidu and took it, he was added as General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and left overseer of the campaign grand marshal with discretionary authority.
translations.idiomatic: At the storming of Yidu he was made General of the Dragon-Tiger Guard and left overseer of the campaign grand marshal with discretionary powers.

sentences.zh: 師還，駐謙謙州，即古烏孫國也。

translations.literal: When the army returned it encamped at Qianqian Prefecture, the ancient Wusun state.
translations.idiomatic: On the return march the army encamped at Qianqian Prefecture—the ancient land of the Wusun.

sentences.zh: 歲己丑，將所部及契丹、女直、唐兀、漢兵，攻斡脫剌兒城。

translations.literal: In the jichou year he led his command together with Khitan, Jurchen, Tangut, and Han troops to attack the city of Otural.
translations.idiomatic: In the jichou year he led his command with Khitan, Jurchen, Tangut, and Han troops against the city of Otural.

sentences.zh: 塔剌渾督諸軍，穴城先入，破之，即軍中拜元帥，改銀青榮祿大夫。

translations.literal: Talahun directed the armies, tunneled into the city and entered first, broke it, and was thereupon in the army made marshal and changed to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.
translations.idiomatic: Talahun directed the assault, tunneled into the city, and broke in first. The army thereupon made him marshal and promoted him to Grand Master of Splendid Happiness with Silver Seal.

sentences.zh: 從睿宗入散關，略關外四州，經興元，渡漢江，略唐、鄧、申、裕諸州，鼓行而東，河南平。

translations.literal: He followed Ruizong through San Pass, swept the four prefectures outside the pass, passed through Xingyuan, crossed the Han River, swept Tang, Deng, Shen, and Yu prefectures, marched east with drums beating, and Henan was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Tolui through San Pass, took the four outer prefectures, passed Xingyuan, crossed the Han, swept Tang, Deng, Shen, and Yu, marched east with drums beating, and pacified Henan.

sentences.zh: 陞金紫光祿大夫、緫領都元帥。

translations.literal: He was advanced to Golden Pacifier Grand Master of the Palace and overall commander of the grand marshalate.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted to Golden Pacifier Grand Master of the Palace and overall commander of the grand marshalate.

sentences.zh: 從大帥太赤攻徐、邳，平之。

translations.literal: He followed the great commander Tai Chi in attacking Xu and Pi and pacified them.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the great commander Tai Chi in taking Xu and Pi.

sentences.zh: 十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixteenth year he died.

sentences.zh: 子抄兒赤襲，從諸王也孫哥、塔察兒南征。

translations.literal: His son Chao'erchi inherited and followed the princes Yesünke and Tachar on the southern campaign.
translations.idiomatic: His son Chao'erchi succeeded and followed Princes Yesünke and Tachar on the southern campaign.

sentences.zh: 戊午，卒於軍。

translations.literal: In the wuwu year he died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuwu year he died in the field.

sentences.zh: 子冀驢襲，卒。

translations.literal: His son Jilü inherited and died.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jilü succeeded and died.

sentences.zh: 弟六十八襲。

translations.literal: His younger brother Liushiba inherited.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother Liushiba succeeded.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，諸軍圍襄樊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan the various armies besieged Xiang-Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 the armies besieged Xiangyang and Fancheng.

sentences.zh: 九年，六十八帥所部戍駱駝嶺一字城，立砲樊城南，不發，以怠敵心，俄帥銳卒突出，攻其城西，破之。

translations.literal: In the ninth year Liushiba led his command to garrison the Yizicheng at Luotuo Ridge, set up artillery south of Fancheng but did not fire, to lull the enemy; soon he led picked troops in a sudden thrust and attacked the west of the city and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year Liushiba garrisoned Yizicheng at Luotuo Ridge, placed artillery south of Fancheng but held fire to lull the enemy, then led picked troops in a sudden assault on the west wall and broke through.

sentences.zh: 以功賜銀幣、鞍馬、弓矢。

translations.literal: For merit he was granted silver coins, saddles and horses, and bows and arrows.
translations.idiomatic: For this he received silver, horses, saddles, and bows and arrows.

sentences.zh: 十一年，諸軍南征，渡江。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year the various armies campaigned south and crossed the Yangtze.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year the armies marched south and crossed the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 明年，加宣武將軍。

translations.literal: The following year he was added as Manifest Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he was made Manifest Martial General.

sentences.zh: 宋常州守臣姚，堅守不下，六十八發砲摧其城壁，以納諸軍。

translations.literal: The Song defender of Changzhou, Yao Yan, held firm and would not fall; Liushiba fired artillery and shattered the city walls to admit the armies.
translations.idiomatic: The Song commander of Changzhou, Yao Yan, held out stubbornly. Liushiba battered the walls with artillery and opened the city to the army.

sentences.zh: 宋援兵突至，力戰却之。

translations.literal: Song relief troops suddenly arrived; he fought fiercely and drove them back.
translations.idiomatic: When Song reinforcements arrived suddenly, he fought them off.

sentences.zh: 常州既克，帥府令緫新附砲手軍。

translations.literal: After Changzhou was taken the marshal's headquarters ordered him to command the newly submitted artillery troops.
translations.idiomatic: After Changzhou fell the marshal's headquarters put him in command of the newly submitted artillery.

sentences.zh: 臨安降，加懷遠大將軍，從諸軍追宋二王至海，下三十餘城。

translations.literal: When Lin'an surrendered he was advanced to Grand Far-Reaching General and followed the armies in pursuing the two Song princes to the sea, taking more than thirty cities.
translations.idiomatic: When Lin'an surrendered he became Grand Far-Reaching General and pursued the two Song princes to the sea, taking more than thirty cities.

sentences.zh: 十四年，加昭勇大將軍。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was added as Illustrious Valor General.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he was made Illustrious Valor General.

sentences.zh: 十五年，領南軍精銳者入衛，加輔國上將軍。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he led the picked elite of the southern army into palace guard service and was added as General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he brought the southern army's elite into palace guard service and was made General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 十八年，論功，授奉國上將軍，管領砲手軍都元帥。

translations.literal: In the eighteenth year, merit was assessed and he was granted General Who Serves the State and made grand marshal commanding artillery troops.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighteenth year he was made General Who Serves the State and grand marshal of the artillery.

sentences.zh: 二十年，罷都元帥，更授砲手軍匠萬戶，佩三珠虎符。

translations.literal: In the twentieth year the grand marshalate was abolished; he was again appointed myriarch of artillery troops and artisans, wearing a three-pearl tiger tally.
translations.idiomatic: In the twentieth year the grand marshalate was abolished; he became myriarch of artillery and artisans with a three-pearl tiger tally.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year he died.

sentences.zh: 奧敦世英

translations.literal: Aodun Shiying
translations.idiomatic: Aodun Shiying

sentences.zh: 奧敦世英，女真人也。

translations.literal: Aodun Shiying was a Jurchen.
translations.idiomatic: Aodun Shiying was a Jurchen.

sentences.zh: 其先世仕金，為淄州刺史。

translations.literal: His forebears had served the Jin as prefect of Zi Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His ancestors had served the Jin as prefect of Zi.

sentences.zh: 歲癸酉，太祖兵下山東，淄州民奉世英及弟保和迎降，皆授以萬戶。

translations.literal: In the guiyou year, when Taizu's army descended into Shandong, the people of Zi Prefecture presented Shiying and his younger brother Baohe to welcome and submit; both were appointed myriarchs.
translations.idiomatic: In the guiyou year, when Genghis Khan's army entered Shandong, the people of Zi presented Shiying and his brother Baohe in surrender. Both were made myriarchs.

sentences.zh: 世英倜儻有武略，由萬戶遷德興府尹，時金經略使苗道潤，率衆欲復山西。

translations.literal: Shiying was unconventional and had military strategy; from myriarch he was transferred to administrator of Dexing Prefecture; at that time the Jin commissioner Miao Daoyun led troops wishing to recover Shanxi.
translations.idiomatic: Shiying was bold and strategic. Promoted from myriarch to administrator of Dexing, he faced the Jin commissioner Miao Daoyun, who marched to recover Shanxi.

sentences.zh: 世英與戰，克之，將盡殺所俘，其母責之曰：「汝華族也，畏死而降，此卒伍爾，驅之死戰，何忍殺之耶！」

translations.literal: Shiying fought him and defeated him; he was about to kill all the captives; his mother rebuked him, saying: "You are of a civilized clan—you feared death and submitted; these are mere soldiers whom you drove to fight to the death—how can you bear to kill them!"
translations.idiomatic: He defeated Miao Daoyun and was about to slaughter the prisoners. His mother rebuked him: "You are of a civilized house and submitted from fear of death. These men were only common soldiers driven to fight—how can you bear to kill them?"

sentences.zh: 遂止。

translations.literal: He thereupon stopped.
translations.idiomatic: He stopped.

sentences.zh: 世英從數騎巡部定襄，卒於軍。

translations.literal: Shiying with several horsemen patrolled Dingxiang district and died in the army.
translations.idiomatic: While patrolling Dingxiang with a few horsemen, he died in service.

sentences.zh: 保和由萬戶陞昭勇大將軍、德興府元帥，錫虎符，改雄州緫管。

translations.literal: Baohe from myriarch was promoted to Illustrious Valor General and marshal of Dexing Prefecture, granted a tiger tally, and changed to overall commander of Xiong Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Baohe rose from myriarch to Illustrious Valor General and marshal of Dexing, received a tiger tally, and became overall commander of Xiong Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 尋以元帥領真定、保定、順德諸道農事，凡辟田二十餘萬畝。

translations.literal: Soon as marshal he oversaw agriculture in the circuits of Zhending, Baoding, and Shunde, opening fields totaling more than two hundred thousand mu.
translations.idiomatic: As marshal he oversaw farming in Zhending, Baoding, and Shunde, reclaiming more than two hundred thousand mu.

sentences.zh: 改真定路勸農事，兼領諸署，賜居第、戎器、裘馬，給戶，食其租。

translations.literal: He was changed to agricultural commissioner of the Zhending circuit, concurrently overseeing various offices; he was granted a residence, weapons, furs and horses, and households whose rent he consumed.
translations.idiomatic: He became agricultural commissioner of Zhending, with concurrent oversight of several offices, a residence, arms, furs and horses, and rent-yielding households.

sentences.zh: 年五十六，致仕。

translations.literal: Aged fifty-six, he retired from office.
translations.idiomatic: He retired at fifty-six.

sentences.zh: 保和四子：希愷，希元，希魯，希尹。

translations.literal: Baohe had four sons: Xikai, Xiyuan, Xilu, and Xiyin.
translations.idiomatic: Baohe had four sons: Xikai, Xiyuan, Xilu, and Xiyin.

sentences.zh: 希愷襲勸農事，皇太后錫以錦服，曰：「無墜汝世業。」

translations.literal: Xikai inherited the agricultural commission; the empress dowager granted him brocade robes, saying: "Do not fall short of your family's vocation."
translations.idiomatic: Xikai inherited the agricultural post. The empress dowager gave him brocade robes and said, "Do not disgrace your family's calling."

sentences.zh: 郡縣有水旱，必力請蠲租調，民賴之。

translations.literal: When prefectures and districts had flood or drought he always pressed hard to request remission of rent and tax; the people relied on him.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever districts suffered flood or drought he pressed for tax relief, and the people relied on him.

sentences.zh: 南征時，置軍儲倉于汴、衛，歲輸河北諸路粟以實之，分冬月三限，失終限者死，吏徵斂舞法，民甚苦之。

translations.literal: On the southern campaign military granaries were set up at Bian and Wei; each year grain from the Hebei circuits was transported to fill them, divided into three winter deadlines—failure at the final deadline meant death; officials exacted by twisting the law and the people suffered greatly.
translations.idiomatic: For the southern campaign granaries were set up at Bian and Wei, filled yearly with Hebei grain under three winter deadlines—missing the last meant death. Officials twisted the law in collection and the people suffered.

sentences.zh: 希愷知其弊，蠲煩苛而民不擾。

translations.literal: Xikai knew these abuses and abolished vexatious exactions so the people were not disturbed.
translations.idiomatic: Xikai knew the abuses and cut the harsh levies without disturbing the people.

sentences.zh: 尋以勸農使兼知冀州。

translations.literal: Soon he was made agricultural commissioner concurrently administering Ji Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became agricultural commissioner and concurrent administrator of Ji Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 希愷至，為束約，健訟之俗為變。

translations.literal: When Xikai arrived he set binding agreements and the litigious custom changed.
translations.idiomatic: When he arrived he imposed clear rules and the lawsuit-ridden district changed.

sentences.zh: 蒙古軍取民田牧，久不歸，希愷悉奪歸之，軍無怨言。

translations.literal: Mongol troops had taken commoners' fields for pasture and long did not return them; Xikai recovered them all and the army had no complaint.
translations.idiomatic: Mongol troops had seized civilian fields for pasture and kept them. Xikai recovered them all without arousing complaint from the army.

sentences.zh: 至元二年，遷順天治中。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to administrative vice-director of Shuntian.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 2 he became administrative vice-director of Shuntian.

sentences.zh: 三月，改順德。

translations.literal: In the third month he was changed to Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he was moved to Shunde.

sentences.zh: 又踰月，陞知河中府，秩滿歸調。

translations.literal: After another month he was advanced to administrator of Hezhong Prefecture; when his term ended he returned for reassignment.
translations.idiomatic: A month later he was made administrator of Hezhong. When his term ended he returned for reassignment.

sentences.zh: 時阿合馬專政，官以賄成，希愷不往見之，降武德將軍，知景州，數月卒。

translations.literal: At that time Ahmad monopolized government and offices were won by bribery; Xikai did not go to see him and was demoted to Martial Virtue General and administrator of Jing Prefecture; he died several months later.
translations.idiomatic: Ahmad then dominated the government and offices were bought. Xikai refused to visit him and was demoted to Martial Virtue General and administrator of Jing Prefecture; he died within months.

sentences.zh: 希元，彰德漕運使。

translations.literal: Xiyuan was transport commissioner of Zhangde.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyuan was transport commissioner of Zhangde.

sentences.zh: 希魯，澧州路緫管。

translations.literal: Xilu was overall administrator of Lizhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Xilu was overall administrator of the Lizhou circuit.

sentences.zh: 希尹，中統三年，李璮叛濟南，世祖命丞相史天澤討之。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong, Li Tan rebelled at Jinan; Shizu ordered Chancellor Shi Tianze to suppress him.
translations.idiomatic: In the third Zhongtong year, when Li Tan rebelled at Jinan, Kublai ordered Chancellor Shi Tianze to suppress him.

sentences.zh: 希尹謁天澤，面陳利害，願擊賊自效。

translations.literal: Xiyin visited Tianze, stated the advantages and disadvantages face to face, and wished to strike the rebels and offer his service.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin visited Tianze, explained the situation frankly, and asked to fight the rebels.

sentences.zh: 試其騎射，壯之，命充真定路行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Tianze tested his mounted archery, admired him, and ordered him to serve as campaign chiliarch of the Zhending circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Tianze tested his archery on horseback, was impressed, and made him campaign chiliarch of Zhending.

sentences.zh: 與賊戰，矢無虛發，賊敗走入城中，諸王哈必赤賞銀五十兩。

translations.literal: In battle with the rebels his arrows never missed; the rebels were defeated and fled into the city; Prince Khubilchi rewarded him with fifty taels of silver.
translations.idiomatic: In battle his arrows never missed. The rebels broke and fled into the city. Prince Khubilchi gave him fifty taels of silver.

sentences.zh: 希尹請築外城圍之，深溝高壘，俟其糧絕，不戰而坐待其困，天澤從之。

translations.literal: Xiyin requested building an outer wall to besiege them, with deep moats and high ramparts, waiting until their grain was exhausted and not fighting but sitting to await their distress; Tianze followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Xiyin proposed an outer encirclement with deep moats and high walls, starving the city rather than assaulting it. Tianze agreed.

sentences.zh: 璮既就擒，至元十一年，樞密錄其功，自右衛經歷，六遷至同知廣東道宣慰司事，卒。

translations.literal: When Tan was captured, in the eleventh year of Zhiyuan the Bureau of Military Affairs recorded his merit; from experience in the Right Guard he rose through six promotions to associate administrator of the Guangdong pacification commission and died.
translations.idiomatic: After Tan was taken, his merit was recorded in Zhiyuan 11. From a post in the Right Guard he rose through six promotions to associate administrator of the Guangdong pacification commission and died.

sentences.zh: 田雄字毅英，北京人也。

translations.literal: Tian Xiong, courtesy name Yiying, was a native of Beiping.
translations.idiomatic: Tian Xiong, styled Yiying, came from Beiping.

sentences.zh: 幼孤，能樹立，以驍勇善騎射知名，金末署軍都統。

translations.literal: Orphaned in youth, he could establish himself; he was famed for fierceness and skill in mounted archery; in the late Jin he was appointed army commander.
translations.idiomatic: Orphaned young, he made his own way, famed for valor and mounted archery. In the late Jin he was made army commander.

sentences.zh: 歲辛未，太祖軍至北京，雄率衆出降。

translations.literal: In the xinwei year Taizu's army reached Beiping; Xiong led the multitude out to submit.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year Genghis Khan's army reached Beiping and Tian Xiong surrendered with his followers.

sentences.zh: 太祖以雄隸太師、國王木華黎麾下，從征興中、廣寧諸郡，定府州縣二十有九，平錦州張鯨兄弟之亂，從攻柏鄉、邢、相。

translations.literal: Taizu placed Xiong under the Grand Tutor and King Muqali; he followed campaigns in Xingzhong, Guangning, and other commanderies, settled twenty-nine prefectures and districts, pacified the rebellion of Zhang Jing and his brothers at Jin Prefecture, and followed attacks on Baixiang, Xing, and Xiang.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan placed him under Muqali. He campaigned in Xingzhong, Guangning, and elsewhere, settled twenty-nine prefectures and districts, quelled the Zhang Jing brothers at Jinzhou, and fought at Baixiang, Xing, and Xiang.

sentences.zh: 辛巳，從攻鄜、坊、綏、葭諸州有功，木華黎承制授雄隰、吉州刺史，兼鎮戎軍節度使，行都元帥府事，平汾西霍山諸柵。

translations.literal: In the xinsi year he followed in attacking Fu, Fang, Sui, and Jia prefectures with merit; Muqali, acting by commission, appointed Xiong prefect of Xi and Ji and military commissioner of Zhenrong Army, acting grand marshal's headquarters, pacifying the stockades of Huoshan west of Fen.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinsi year he attacked Fu, Fang, Sui, and Jia with merit. Muqali made him prefect of Xi and Ji, commissioner of the Zhenrong Army, and acting marshal of the west, pacifying stockades west of Fen at Huoshan.

sentences.zh: 壬午，以木華黎命，授河中帥，聽石天應節制。

translations.literal: In the renwu year, by Muqali's order, he was appointed commander of Hezhong and placed under Shi Tianying's control.
translations.idiomatic: In the renwu year Muqali appointed him commander of Hezhong under Shi Tianying.

sentences.zh: 太宗時，從攻西和、興元諸州；

translations.literal: In Taizong's time he followed attacks on Xihe, Xingyuan, and other prefectures;
translations.idiomatic: Under Ögedei he attacked Xihe, Xingyuan, and other prefectures;

sentences.zh: 又從攻夔、萬諸州。

translations.literal: again he followed attacks on Kui and Wan prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: and again Kui and Wan.

sentences.zh: 論功尤最，賜金符，授行軍千戶，召為御前先鋒。

translations.literal: His merit was judged supreme; he was granted a gold tally, appointed campaign chiliarch, and summoned as vanguard before the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: His merit was judged supreme. He received a gold tally, became campaign chiliarch, and was summoned as imperial vanguard.

sentences.zh: 頃之，使攻破楨州雷家堡。

translations.literal: Shortly thereafter he was sent to storm Leijia Stockade in Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was sent to storm Leijia Stockade in Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 奉旨招納河南降附，得戶十三萬七千有奇，民皆按堵，而別部將校，縱兵虜掠，民惶懼悔降，雄力為救護，至出己財與之，民得免於害。

translations.literal: By imperial order he induced submission in Henan and obtained households numbering one hundred thirty-seven thousand odd; the people all remained secure; but other commanders and officers let their troops plunder captives; the people feared and regretted submission; Xiong strove to protect them, even bringing out his own wealth to give them, and the people escaped harm.
translations.idiomatic: By imperial order he brought in Henan submitters totaling 137,000-odd households and kept them secure. When other commanders let troops loot them, the people feared they had erred in submitting. Tian Xiong protected them, even paying from his own wealth, and saved them from harm.

sentences.zh: 癸巳，授鎮撫陝西緫管京兆等路事。

translations.literal: In the guisi year he was appointed pacification commissioner overall administering Jingzhao and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the guisi year he was made pacification commissioner over Jingzhao and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 時關中苦於兵革，郡縣蕭然。

translations.literal: At that time Guanzhong suffered bitterly from war; prefectures and districts were desolate.
translations.idiomatic: Guanzhong had been ravaged by war; the districts lay waste.

sentences.zh: 雄披荊棘，立官府，開陳禍福，招徠四山堡寨之未降者，獲其人，皆慰遣之，由是來附者日衆。

translations.literal: Xiong cleared brambles, established government offices, set forth fortune and misfortune, and induced the stockades of the four mountains not yet submitted; when he obtained their people he all comforted and sent them away; thereby those who came to submit daily increased.
translations.idiomatic: He cleared the land, set up offices, explained the stakes to unsubmitting mountain stockades, comforted those who came in, and daily grew the number of submitters.

sentences.zh: 雄乃教民力田，京兆大治。

translations.literal: Xiong then taught the people to labor in the fields and Jingzhao was greatly ordered.
translations.idiomatic: He taught the people to farm, and Jingzhao was greatly restored.

sentences.zh: 事聞，賜金符。

translations.literal: When the matter was reported he was granted a gold tally.
translations.idiomatic: When this was reported he received a gold tally.

sentences.zh: 定宗時，入覲于和林。

translations.literal: In Dingzong's time he had audience at Karakorum.
translations.idiomatic: Under Güyük he had audience at Karakorum.

sentences.zh: 以疾卒，年五十八。

translations.literal: He died of illness, aged fifty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: He died of illness at fifty-eight.

sentences.zh: 後追封西秦王。

translations.literal: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of the Western Qin.
translations.idiomatic: Later he was posthumously enfeoffed as King of the Western Qin.

sentences.zh: 子八人，大明，襲職，知京兆等路都緫管府事。

translations.literal: He had eight sons; Daming inherited the post and administered the overall headquarters of Jingzhao and other circuits.
translations.idiomatic: He had eight sons. Daming succeeded and governed the overall headquarters of Jingzhao and neighboring circuits.

sentences.zh: 張拔都

translations.literal: Zhang Badu
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Badu

sentences.zh: 張拔都，昌平人。

translations.literal: Zhang Badu was a native of Changping.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Badu came from Changping.

sentences.zh: 歲辛未，太祖南征，拔都率衆來附，願為前驅，遂留備宿衛。

translations.literal: In the xinwei year Taizu campaigned south; Badu led the multitude to submit and wished to serve as vanguard; he was thereupon retained for palace guard duty.
translations.idiomatic: In the xinwei year, on Genghis Khan's southern campaign, Badu submitted and asked to serve as vanguard. He was kept for palace guard duty.

sentences.zh: 從近臣漢都虎西征回紇、河西諸蕃，道隴、蜀入洛，屢戰，流矢中頰不少却。

translations.literal: He followed the close attendant Handuhu on the western campaign against the Huihui and the various tribes of Hexi, by way of Long and Shu entering Luo, fought repeatedly, was struck in the cheek by stray arrows but did not retreat.
translations.idiomatic: He followed the close attendant Handuhu west against the Muslim lands and Hexi tribes, marching through Long and Shu into Luoyang. Struck in the cheek by arrows, he did not retreat.

sentences.zh: 帝聞而壯之，賜名拔都，自是漢都虎亦專任之。

translations.literal: The emperor heard and admired this, granted the name Badu, and from then on Handuhu also relied on him exclusively.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired this, gave him the name Badu, and Handuhu thereafter relied on him exclusively.

sentences.zh: 甲午，金亡，以漢都虎為砲手諸色軍民人匠都元帥，守真定。

translations.literal: In the jiawu year the Jin perished; Handuhu was made grand marshal of artillery and naval forces, military and civilian personnel, and craftsmen of every category, garrisoning Zhending.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiawu year, when the Jin fell, Handuhu became grand marshal of artillery, sailors, civilians, and artisans, garrisoning Zhending.

sentences.zh: 漢都虎卒，無子，以拔都代之。

translations.literal: When Handuhu died without sons, Badu replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: When Handuhu died childless, Badu replaced him.

sentences.zh: 及漢都虎兄子贍闍少長，拔都請于朝，歸其政而終老焉。

translations.literal: When Handuhu's elder brother's son Shanchan grew up, Badu requested of the court and returned the government to him, ending his days in retirement.
translations.idiomatic: When Handuhu's nephew Shanchan came of age, Badu petitioned the court, returned command to him, and retired.

sentences.zh: 子忙古台，從憲宗攻蜀釣魚山、苦竹二壘，冒犯矢石，屢挫而不沮，遂以勇敢聞。

translations.literal: His son Mangutai followed Xianzong in attacking Diaoyu Mountain and Kuzhu stockades in Shu; he braved arrows and stones, was repeatedly thwarted but not discouraged, and thereby became famed for courage.
translations.idiomatic: His son Mangutai followed Möngke against Diaoyu Mountain and Kuzhu stockades in Shu, braved arrows and stones without discouragement, and won fame for courage.

sentences.zh: 中統元年，賜銀符，預議砲手軍府事。

translations.literal: In the first year of Zhongtong he was granted a silver tally and took part in deliberations of the artillery headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: In the first Zhongtong year he received a silver tally and joined deliberations at the artillery headquarters.

sentences.zh: 尋易金符，為行軍千戶，從征襄樊有功，卒。

translations.literal: Soon it was changed to a gold tally; he became campaign chiliarch, followed the Xiang-Fan campaign with merit, and died.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he received a gold tally, became campaign chiliarch, distinguished himself at Xiang-Fan, and died.

sentences.zh: 子世澤襲，從丞相伯顏南征，大小十餘戰，皆有功。

translations.literal: His son Shize inherited and followed Chancellor Bayan on the southern campaign; in more than ten battles large and small he all had merit.
translations.idiomatic: His son Shize succeeded and followed Chancellor Bayan south in more than ten engagements with merit.

sentences.zh: 又從平廣西。

translations.literal: He again followed in pacifying Guangxi.
translations.idiomatic: He also helped pacify Guangxi.

sentences.zh: 明年，收瓊、萬諸州，拜宣武將軍、行軍緫管。

translations.literal: The following year he recovered Qiong and Wan prefectures and was appointed Manifest Martial General and campaign overall commander.
translations.idiomatic: The next year he recovered Qiong and Wan and was made Manifest Martial General and campaign commander.

sentences.zh: 未幾，遷副萬戶，加明威將軍。

translations.literal: Before long he was transferred to deputy myriarch and added as Illustrious Might General.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he became deputy myriarch and Illustrious Might General.

sentences.zh: 從鎮南王脫歡伐交趾，既還，及再舉，將校舊嘗往者，許留恤之。

translations.literal: He followed the Prince of Pacifying the South Togan in the campaign against Annam; after returning, on the second expedition, commanders and officers who had gone before were permitted to remain for relief.
translations.idiomatic: He followed Prince Togan against Annam. On the second expedition veterans of the first were allowed to stay behind for relief.

sentences.zh: 有脫歡者，當行，適病，不能起，世澤曰：「吾祖父以武勇稱，吾蒙其餘澤，荷國厚恩，當輸忠王室，增光前人，豈可苟為自安計耶！」

translations.literal: There was a Togan who should have gone but happened to fall ill and could not rise; Shize said: "My grandfather and father were famed for martial valor; I receive the remnant grace of their legacy and bear the state's thick favor—I ought to offer loyalty to the royal house and add glory to my forebears—how can I seek only my own ease!"
translations.idiomatic: A man named Togan should have gone but fell ill. Shize said, "My forebears were famed for valor. I owe the state a great debt. How can I seek only my own comfort?"

sentences.zh: 力請代之，凱還，人服其義云。

translations.literal: He forcefully requested to replace him; returning in triumph, people admired his righteousness.
translations.idiomatic: He insisted on going in his place. On the victorious return people admired his sense of duty.

sentences.zh: 張榮，清州人，後徙鄢陵。

translations.literal: Zhang Rong was a native of Qing Prefecture and later moved to Yanling.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Rong came from Qing Prefecture and later moved to Yanling.

sentences.zh: 歲甲戌，從太保明安降，太祖賜虎符，授懷遠大將軍、元帥左都監。

translations.literal: In the jiaxu year he followed the Grand Tutor Ming'an in submission; Taizu granted a tiger tally and appointed him Grand Far-Reaching General and left overseer of the grand marshal.
translations.idiomatic: In the jiaxu year he submitted with Grand Tutor Ming'an. Genghis Khan gave him a tiger tally and made him Grand Far-Reaching General and left overseer of the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 乙亥正月，奉旨略東平、益都諸郡。

translations.literal: In the first month of the yihai year, by imperial order he swept Dongping, Yidu, and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of yihai he swept Dongping, Yidu, and other commanderies by imperial order.

sentences.zh: 戊寅，領軍匠，從太祖征西域諸國。

translations.literal: In the wuyin year he led artisan troops and followed Taizu in campaigning against the states of the Western Regions.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuyin year he led artisan troops on Genghis Khan's Western Regions campaign.

sentences.zh: 庚辰八月，至西域莫蘭河，不能涉。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the gengchen year they reached the Moran River in the Western Regions and could not cross.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of gengchen they reached the Moran River in the west and could not cross.

sentences.zh: 太祖召問濟河之策，榮請造舟。

translations.literal: Taizu summoned and asked the strategy for crossing the river; Rong requested to build boats.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan asked how to cross. Rong proposed building boats.

sentences.zh: 太祖復問：「舟卒難成，濟師當在何時？」

translations.literal: Taizu again asked: "Boats are hard to complete quickly—when should the army cross?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked again, "Boats take time—when can the army cross?"

sentences.zh: 榮請以一月為期，乃督工匠，造船百艘，遂濟河。

translations.literal: Rong requested one month as the term; he then supervised craftsmen, built a hundred boats, and crossed the river.
translations.idiomatic: Rong asked for one month, supervised a hundred boats, and crossed.

sentences.zh: 太祖嘉其能，而賞其功，賜名兀速赤。

translations.literal: Taizu praised his ability and rewarded his merit, granting the name Usuchi.
translations.idiomatic: Genghis Khan praised his skill, rewarded him, and gave him the name Usuchi.

sentences.zh: 癸未七月，陞鎮國上將軍、砲水手元帥。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the guiwei year he was advanced to General Who Secures the State and marshal of artillery and naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of guiwei he became General Who Secures the State and marshal of artillery and naval forces.

sentences.zh: 甲申七月，從征河西。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the jiashen year he followed the campaign in Hexi.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of jiashen he campaigned in Hexi.

sentences.zh: 乙酉，從征關西五路。

translations.literal: In the yiyou year he followed the campaign in the five circuits of Guanxi.
translations.idiomatic: In yiyou he campaigned in the five Guanxi circuits.

sentences.zh: 十月，攻鳳翔，砲傷右髀，帝命賜銀三十錠，養病於雲內州。

translations.literal: In the tenth month he attacked Fengxiang; artillery wounded his right thigh; the emperor ordered thirty ingots of silver granted and convalescence in Yunnei Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month he attacked Fengxiang. Artillery wounded his right thigh. The emperor gave him thirty silver ingots and sent him to convalesce at Yunnei.

sentences.zh: 庚寅七月卒，年七十三。

translations.literal: In the seventh month of the gengyin year he died, aged seventy-three.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh month of gengyin he died at seventy-three.

sentences.zh: 子奴婢，襲佩虎符、砲水手元帥，領諸色軍匠。

translations.literal: His son Nubi inherited wearing the tiger tally, marshal of artillery and naval forces, commanding military and artisan troops of every category.
translations.idiomatic: His son Nubi succeeded with the tiger tally as marshal of artillery, commanding troops and artisans of every kind.

sentences.zh: 太宗伐金，命由關西小口，收附金昌州等郡。

translations.literal: Taizong campaigned against the Jin and ordered him by the small pass of Guanxi to receive submission of Jinchang Prefecture and other commanderies.
translations.idiomatic: Ögedei attacked the Jin and ordered him through the Guanxi narrow pass to receive the submission of Jinchang and other prefectures.

sentences.zh: 乙未，金亡。

translations.literal: In the yiwei year the Jin perished.
translations.idiomatic: In the yiwei year the Jin fell.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，授懷遠大將軍。

translations.literal: In the wuxu year he was appointed Grand Far-Reaching General.
translations.idiomatic: In the wuxu year he was made Grand Far-Reaching General.

sentences.zh: 癸卯三月，陞輔國大將軍。

translations.literal: In the third month of the guimao year he was advanced to Grand General Who Assists the State.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month of guimao he became Grand General Who Assists the State.

sentences.zh: 甲辰二月，領蒙古、漢軍，守鈞州。

translations.literal: In the second month of the jiachen year he led Mongol and Han troops garrisoning Jun Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of jiachen he garrisoned Jun Prefecture with Mongol and Han troops.

sentences.zh: 戊申九月，宋兵襲鈞州，奴婢拒戰，大敗宋師。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the wushen year Song troops raided Jun Prefecture; Nubi resisted and inflicted a great defeat on the Song army.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of wushen Song forces raided Jun. Nubi repulsed them and routed the Song army.

sentences.zh: 己酉十一月，復與宋兵戰，流矢中右臂。

translations.literal: In the eleventh month of the jiyou year he again fought Song troops and was struck in the right arm by a stray arrow.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh month of jiyou he fought the Song again and took an arrow in the right arm.

sentences.zh: 中統三年卒，年七十五。

translations.literal: In the third year of Zhongtong he died, aged seventy-five.
translations.idiomatic: He died in the third Zhongtong year at seventy-five.

sentences.zh: 子君佐，襲佩虎符、砲水手元帥，戍蔡州。

translations.literal: His son Junzuo inherited wearing the tiger tally as marshal of artillery and naval forces, garrisoning Caizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His son Junzuo succeeded with the tiger tally as artillery marshal, garrisoning Caizhou.

sentences.zh: 五年，都元帥阿朮，命將砲手兵攻襄陽。

translations.literal: In the fifth year the grand marshal Aju ordered him to lead artillery troops to attack Xiangyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifth year Grand Marshal Aju ordered him to lead artillery against Xiangyang.

sentences.zh: 至元八年，調守襄陽一字城、橐駝嶺，攻南門牛角堡，破之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhiyuan he was transferred to garrison Yizicheng and Luotuo Ridge at Xiangyang, attacked the Ox-Horn stockade at the south gate, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 8 he garrisoned Yizicheng and Luotuo Ridge at Xiangyang, assaulted the Ox-Horn stockade at the south gate, and took it.

sentences.zh: 攻樊城，親立砲摧其角樓，樊城破。

translations.literal: Attacking Fancheng he personally set up artillery and shattered the corner tower; Fancheng was broken.
translations.idiomatic: At Fancheng he personally deployed artillery, shattered the corner tower, and the city fell.

sentences.zh: 十年，襄陽降。

translations.literal: In the tenth year Xiangyang surrendered.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Xiangyang surrendered.

sentences.zh: 參政阿魯海牙以宋降將呂文煥入朝，奉旨召蒙古、漢人萬戶凡二十人陛見，各以功受賜。

translations.literal: Vice Administrator Aruhaigi brought the Song surrendered general Lü Wenhuan to court; by imperial order twenty Mongol and Han myriarchs were summoned to audience and each received rewards according to merit.
translations.idiomatic: Vice Administrator Aruhaigi brought the surrendered Song general Lü Wenhuan to court. Twenty Mongol and Han myriarchs were summoned to audience and rewarded according to merit.

sentences.zh: 帝親諭之，令還鎮。

translations.literal: The emperor personally instructed them and ordered them to return to their garrisons.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor addressed them in person and ordered them back to their posts.

sentences.zh: 十一年，從軍下漢江，至沙洋。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he followed the army down the Han River as far as Shayang.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he marched down the Han to Shayang.

sentences.zh: 丞相伯顏命率砲手軍攻其北面，火砲焚城中民舍幾盡，遂破之，賜以良馬、金鞍、金段。

translations.literal: Chancellor Bayan ordered him to lead artillery troops to attack the north face; fire artillery burned the commoners' dwellings in the city nearly to nothing and in the end it was stormed; he was granted fine horses, gold saddles, and gold brocade.
translations.idiomatic: Chancellor Bayan ordered him to batter the north face. Fire artillery burned nearly all the dwellings in the city before it fell. He received fine horses, gold saddles, and brocade.

sentences.zh: 又以火砲攻陽邏堡，破之。

translations.literal: Again with fire artillery he attacked Yangluo Stockade and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: He also took Yangluo Stockade with fire artillery.

sentences.zh: 十二年，從大軍與宋將孫虎臣戰于丁家洲，復從丞相阿朮攻揚州，是年冬，又從諸軍破常州。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he followed the great army in fighting the Song general Sun Huchen at Dingjiazhou, again followed Chancellor Aju in attacking Yangzhou, and that winter again followed the various armies in storming Changzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the twelfth year he fought Sun Huchen at Dingjiazhou, joined Aju against Yangzhou, and that winter helped take Changzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年，陞懷遠大將軍，仍砲水手元帥。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year he was advanced to Grand Far-Reaching General, still marshal of artillery and naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year he became Grand Far-Reaching General, still marshal of artillery.

sentences.zh: 秋，君佐屯軍真、揚間，絕宋糧道。

translations.literal: In autumn Junzuo encamped his army between Zhen and Yang, cutting the Song grain route.
translations.idiomatic: That autumn he camped between Zhen and Yang and cut the Song supply line.

sentences.zh: 宋制置李庭芝、都統姜才棄城走，揚州平，以君佐為安慶府安撫司軍民達魯花赤。

translations.literal: The Song commissioner Li Tingzhi and commander-in-chief Jiang Cai abandoned the city and fled; Yangzhou was pacified; Junzuo was made darughachi of the Anqing pacification commission for military and civilians.
translations.idiomatic: Li Tingzhi and Jiang Cai fled Yangzhou. After its fall Junzuo became darughachi of the Anqing pacification commission.

sentences.zh: 十四年春，安慶野人原及司空山天堂賊，將攻安慶，君佐密察知之。

translations.literal: In the spring of the fourteenth year the wild men of Yeren and the Tiantang bandits of Sikong Mountain in Anqing were about to attack Anqing; Junzuo secretly observed and knew it.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of the fourteenth year bandits from Yeren and Sikong Mountain threatened Anqing. Junzuo detected the plot in secret.

sentences.zh: 時城中軍僅數百人，君佐命搤賊出沒要道，賊不敢入，乃寇黃州。

translations.literal: At that time there were only several hundred troops in the city; Junzuo ordered them to block the bandits' routes of egress and ingress; the bandits dared not enter and then raided Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The city held only a few hundred troops. He blocked the bandits' routes, they dared not enter Anqing, and turned to raid Huangzhou.

sentences.zh: 行省命君佐率衆復黃州，因以為黃州達魯花赤。

translations.literal: The branch secretariat ordered Junzuo to lead troops to recover Huang Prefecture; thereby he was made darughachi of Huang Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: The regional office ordered him to recover Huangzhou, and he was made its darughachi.

sentences.zh: 十五年，加鎮國上將軍，仍砲水手元帥。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year he was added as General Who Secures the State, still marshal of artillery and naval forces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year he was made General Who Secures the State, still artillery marshal.

sentences.zh: 十九年，命率新附漢軍萬人，修膠西閘壩，以通漕運。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year he was ordered to lead ten thousand newly submitted Han troops to repair the Jiaoxi sluice dam to open grain transport by water.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year he led ten thousand newly submitted Han troops to repair the Jiaoxi sluice for grain transport.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，兼海道運糧事，是年卒。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he concurrently oversaw sea-route grain transport; that year he died.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he also oversaw sea-route grain transport and died that year.

sentences.zh: 趙天錫賁亨

translations.literal: Zhao Tianxi; Benheng
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tianxi (Benheng)

sentences.zh: 趙天錫字受之，冠氏人。

translations.literal: Zhao Tianxi, courtesy name Shouzhi, was a native of Guan Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Zhao Tianxi, styled Shouzhi, came from Guan Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 屬金季兵起，其祖以財雄鄉里，為衆所歸。

translations.literal: When troops arose in the late Jin, his grandfather by wealth dominated the district and was where the multitude turned.
translations.idiomatic: In the late Jin his grandfather's wealth made him leader of the district.

sentences.zh: 貞祐之亂，父林，保冠氏有功，授冠氏丞，俄陞為令。

translations.literal: In the disorder of Zhenyou, his father Lin defended Guan Prefecture with merit and was appointed assistant magistrate of Guan, soon promoted to magistrate.
translations.idiomatic: In the Zhenyou disorders his father Lin defended Guan with merit, became assistant magistrate, and soon magistrate.

sentences.zh: 大安末，天錫入粟佐軍，補修武校尉，監洺水縣酒。

translations.literal: At the end of Da'an, Tianxi contributed grain to support the army, was appointed repair-army company commander, and supervised wine at Ming Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Da'an, Tianxi contributed grain to the army, became repair-army company commander, and supervised wine at Ming Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 太祖遣兵南下，防禦使蘇政以為冠氏令，乃挈縣人壁桃源、天平諸山。

translations.literal: When Taizu sent troops south, Defense Commissioner Su Zheng made him magistrate of Guan; he then led the county people to fortify Taoyuan, Tianping, and other mountains.
translations.idiomatic: When Genghis Khan marched south, Su Zheng made him magistrate of Guan, and he led the people to fortify Taoyuan, Tianping, and other mountains.

sentences.zh: 歲辛巳春，歸行臺東平嚴實。

translations.literal: In the spring of the xinsi year he submitted to Yan Shi of the Eastern Secretariat at Dongping.
translations.idiomatic: In the spring of xinsi he submitted to Yan Shi of the Dongping secretariat.

sentences.zh: 實素知天錫名，遂擢隸帳下，從征上黨，以功授冠氏令，俄遷元帥左都監，兼令如故。

translations.literal: Shi had long known Tianxi's name and thereupon promoted him under his banner; he followed the campaign in Shangdang; for merit he was appointed magistrate of Guan, soon transferred to left overseer of the grand marshal while still holding the magistracy.
translations.idiomatic: Yan Shi knew his reputation, took him into his staff, and campaigned in Shangdang. For merit he became magistrate of Guan, then left overseer of the grand marshal while keeping the magistracy.

sentences.zh: 甲申，宋將彭義斌據大名，冠氏元帥李全降之，人心頗搖。

translations.literal: In the jiashen year the Song general Peng Yibin held Daming; the Guan Prefecture marshal Li Quan submitted to him and hearts were somewhat shaken.
translations.idiomatic: In jiashen the Song general Peng Yibin held Daming. Guan's marshal Li Quan submitted to him and morale wavered.

sentences.zh: 天錫令衆姑少避其鋒，以圖後舉，乃率將佐往依大將孛里海軍。

translations.literal: Tianxi ordered the multitude for the time being to avoid their edge to plan a later move; he then led officers to rely on the great general Bolqai's army.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi had his men avoid the enemy for the moment, then joined the army of the great general Bolqai.

sentences.zh: 未幾，破義斌于真定，授左副元帥、同知大名路兵馬都緫管事。

translations.literal: Before long they defeated Yibin at Zhending; he was appointed left vice marshal and associate overall commander of army and horse of the Daming circuit.
translations.idiomatic: Soon they defeated Yibin at Zhending. Tianxi became left vice marshal and associate commander of Daming's army and horse.

sentences.zh: 李全在大名，結其帥蘇椿，納金河南從宜鄭倜，日以取冠氏為事。

translations.literal: Li Quan was at Daming, joined with his commander Su Chun, and received the Jin Henan commissioner Zheng Ti; daily they took seizing Guan Prefecture as their business.
translations.idiomatic: Li Quan at Daming allied with his commander Su Chun and the Jin commissioner Zheng Ti, pressing daily to take Guan.

sentences.zh: 天錫每戰輒勝，一日，倜自將萬人來攻，天錫率死士乘城，力戰三晝夜，倜度不能下，乘風霾遁去。

translations.literal: Tianxi won in every battle; one day Ti personally led ten thousand men to attack; Tianxi led death-defying troops on the walls and fought fiercely for three days and nights; Ti judged he could not take it and fled away in wind and dust.
translations.idiomatic: Tianxi won repeated engagements. When Zheng Ti attacked with ten thousand men, he held the walls for three days and nights until Ti withdrew in a dust storm.

sentences.zh: 己丑，朝行在所，上便民事，優詔從之。

translations.literal: In the jichou year he had audience at the mobile court and memorialized on convenient matters for the people; an excellent edict approved them.
translations.idiomatic: In jichou he had audience at the mobile court, memorialized on measures to help the people, and received an approving edict.

sentences.zh: 戊戌，征宋，駐兵蘄、黃間，被病還，卒于冠氏，年五十。

translations.literal: In the wuxu year he campaigned against the Song, encamped between Qi and Huang, fell ill and returned, and died at Guan Prefecture, aged fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In wuxu he campaigned against the Song between Qi and Huang, fell ill, returned, and died at Guan at fifty.

sentences.zh: 子六人，賁亨嗣。

translations.literal: He had six sons; Benheng succeeded.
translations.idiomatic: He had six sons; Benheng succeeded.

sentences.zh: 賁亨字文甫，襲行軍千戶。

translations.literal: Benheng, courtesy name Wenfu, inherited as campaign chiliarch.
translations.idiomatic: Benheng, styled Wenfu, succeeded as campaign chiliarch.

sentences.zh: 己未，從國兵渡江攻鄂，有功。

translations.literal: In the jiwei year he followed the national army across the river to attack E and won merit.
translations.idiomatic: In jiwei he crossed the Yangtze with the main army against Ezhou and distinguished himself.

sentences.zh: 至元五年，緫管山東諸翼軍，征宋，攻襄樊。

translations.literal: In the fifth year of Zhiyuan he overall commanded the various wings of Shandong army in the Song campaign and attacked Xiang-Fan.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhiyuan 5 he commanded Shandong wing troops against the Song and besieged Xiang-Fan.

sentences.zh: 賁亨出抄蘄、黃，以五百人拔野人原寫山寨，修白河新城。

translations.literal: Benheng went out to raid Qi and Huang, with five hundred men stormed Yeren and the Xieshan stockade, and repaired Xincheng at Baihe.
translations.idiomatic: He raided Qi and Huang, took Yeren and Xieshan stockade with five hundred men, and rebuilt Xincheng at Baihe.

sentences.zh: 七年，偕元帥劉整朝京師，命為征行千戶，賜金符，及衣帶鞍馬。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he accompanied Marshal Liu Zheng to audience at the capital; he was ordered to serve as campaign chiliarch, granted a gold tally, and given robes, belts, saddles, and horses.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he accompanied Marshal Liu Zheng to court, was made campaign chiliarch, and received a gold tally, robes, belt, saddle, and horses.

sentences.zh: 攻樊城，冒矢石，擁盾先登，破之。

translations.literal: Attacking Fancheng he braved arrows and stones, shielded himself and was first to scale the walls, and broke it.
translations.idiomatic: At Fancheng he braved missiles, shielded himself, was first over the wall, and took the city.

sentences.zh: 十一年，修東、西正陽城。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he repaired the east and west Zhengyang cities.
translations.idiomatic: In the eleventh year he repaired the east and west Zhengyang cities.

sentences.zh: 三月，敗夏貴于淮，益以濟南、汴梁二路新軍。

translations.literal: In the third month he defeated Xia Gui on the Huai and was given additional troops from the newly levied armies of Jinan and Bianliang circuits.
translations.idiomatic: In the third month he defeated Xia Gui on the Huai and received reinforcements from Jinan and Bianliang.

sentences.zh: 十二年正月，從攻鎮江，與宋將孫虎臣、張世傑大戰于焦山，殺掠甚衆。

translations.literal: In the first month of the twelfth year he followed the attack on Zhenjiang and fought a great battle with the Song generals Sun Huchen and Zhang Shijie at Jiao Mountain, killing and seizing very many.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the twelfth year he attacked Zhenjiang and fought Sun Huchen and Zhang Shijie at Jiao Mountain with heavy slaughter.

sentences.zh: 十三年，江南平，以功陞宣武將軍。

translations.literal: In the thirteenth year the Jiangnan region was pacified; for merit he was advanced to Manifest Martial General.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year the south was pacified and he was promoted to Manifest Martial General.

sentences.zh: 十四年，授虎符、懷遠大將軍、處州路緫管府達魯花赤。

translations.literal: In the fourteenth year he was granted a tiger tally, Grand Far-Reaching General, and darughachi of Chuzhou Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourteenth year he received a tiger tally, became Grand Far-Reaching General, and was named darughachi of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 未行，適盜發澉浦，行省檄為招討使，率兵平之。

translations.literal: Before he departed, bandits broke out at Ganpu; the branch secretariat ordered him as pacification commissioner to lead troops and pacify them.
translations.idiomatic: Before he could leave, bandits rose at Ganpu. The regional office made him pacification commissioner to suppress them.

sentences.zh: 未幾，處州青田縣季文龍、章焱殺趙知府以叛，賁亨獲其黨，始知七縣俱反，季文龍自署為兩浙安撫使，據處州天慶觀。

translations.literal: Before long in Qingtian County of Chuzhou Li Wenlong and Zhang Yan killed the Zhao prefect and rebelled; Benheng captured their partisans and only then learned that seven counties had all rebelled; Li Wenlong styled himself pacification commissioner of the two Zhe regions and held Tiantian Temple in Chuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Li Wenlong and Zhang Yan in Qingtian killed the prefect and rebelled. Capturing their agents, Benheng learned seven counties had risen. Li Wenlong styled himself pacification commissioner of the two Zhes and held Tiantian Temple in Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 賁亨率衆圍之，將騎士三百陣于下河門。

translations.literal: Benheng led troops to besiege them and arrayed three hundred horsemen at Xiahemen.
translations.idiomatic: Benheng besieged them and posted three hundred horsemen at Xiahemen.

sentences.zh: 賊出戰，以精騎蹂之，遂棄城突圍散走，斬首三級，賁亨入城，乃招散亡，立官府。

translations.literal: The bandits came out to fight; he trampled them with picked horsemen; they then abandoned the city, broke through the encirclement, and scattered; three heads were beheaded; Benheng entered the city and then summoned the scattered and fugitive and established government offices.
translations.idiomatic: The rebels sallied out; he crushed them with elite cavalry. They abandoned the city and fled. He took three heads, entered the city, gathered the displaced, and restored government.

sentences.zh: 章焱復合二萬衆來攻，陣惡溪南。

translations.literal: Zhang Yan again combined twenty thousand men to attack and arrayed south of Exi.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Yan rallied twenty thousand and formed south of Exi.

sentences.zh: 賁亨分兵拒守，自將精銳亂流衝擊，屬萬戶忽都台以援兵至，自巳至亥，賊方退，文龍溺死。

translations.literal: Benheng divided troops to resist and defend, personally led picked troops to strike across the current in disorder; the myriarch Hudutai arrived with relief troops; from the si hour to the hai hour the bandits only then withdrew; Wenlong drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Benheng divided his force to hold the line and led picked troops across the stream. Myriarch Hudutai arrived with reinforcements. From midday to dusk the rebels withdrew, and Wenlong drowned.

sentences.zh: 忽都台以處即亂山為州，無城壁可恃，且反側，欲屠之，賁亨曰：「我受命來監此郡，賊固可殺，良民何辜！」

translations.literal: Hudutai because Chuzhou was amid chaotic mountains with no city walls to rely on and was still rebellious wished to slaughter it; Benheng said: "I received orders to oversee this commandery—the bandits indeed can be killed, but what crime have the good commoners!"
translations.idiomatic: Hudutai, finding Chuzhou a rebellious mountain district without walls, wished to massacre it. Benheng said, "I was ordered to govern this prefecture. Rebels may be killed, but what have innocent people done?"

sentences.zh: 不從。

translations.literal: He did not follow.
translations.idiomatic: Hudutai did not listen.

sentences.zh: 將士虜掠子女金帛，賁亨捕得倡率者杖之，仍各求所失還之，州民悅服。

translations.literal: The officers and soldiers plundered women, children, gold, and silk; Benheng captured the ringleaders and beat them, then made each seek out what was lost and return it; the people of the prefecture submitted gladly.
translations.idiomatic: Soldiers looted women and goods. Benheng seized the ringleaders, beat them, and made them return what was taken. The people submitted gladly.

sentences.zh: 十五年，龍泉縣張三八合衆二萬，殺慶元縣達魯花赤也速台兒，且屠其家。

translations.literal: In the fifteenth year Zhang Sanba of Longquan County combined twenty thousand men, killed the Qingyuan County darughachi Yasutai'er, and moreover slaughtered his household.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifteenth year Zhang Sanba of Longquan mustered twenty thousand men, killed the Qingyuan darughachi Yasutai'er, and slaughtered his household.

sentences.zh: 賁亨將騎士五百往討，與賊將鄭先鋒、陳壽山三千餘人戰于浮雲鄉，斬首三百餘級。

translations.literal: Benheng led five hundred horsemen to suppress them and fought the bandit generals Zheng Xianfeng and Chen Shoushan with more than three thousand men at Fuyun Township, beheading more than three hundred.
translations.idiomatic: Benheng led five hundred horsemen against them and at Fuyun Township fought the bandit generals Zheng Xianfeng and Chen Shoushan with three thousand men, taking more than three hundred heads.

sentences.zh: 三八軍于縣西，賊三戰俱敗，軍還，賊衆水陸俱設伏，賁亨擇步卒驍悍者使前，賊不敢近。

translations.literal: Sanba encamped west of the county; the bandits were defeated in three battles; when the army returned the bandit multitude set ambushes by land and water; Benheng chose stalwart infantry to go before and the bandits dared not approach.
translations.idiomatic: Sanba camped west of the county. After three defeats the bandits ambushed the return march by land and water. Benheng sent picked infantry ahead and the bandits dared not close in.

sentences.zh: 既而衢州賊陳千二聚二萬人，遂昌葉丙六亦聚三千人助之，賁亨前後斬首三千餘級，悉平之。

translations.literal: Before long the Quzhou bandit Chen Qian'er gathered twenty thousand men, and Suichang's Ye Bingliu also gathered three thousand to aid them; Benheng beheaded more than three thousand in all before and after and pacified them completely.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Chen Qian'er of Quzhou gathered twenty thousand and Ye Bingliu of Suichang three thousand more. Benheng took over three thousand heads in all and pacified them.

sentences.zh: 十七年，改處州路管軍萬戶。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year he was changed to commanding myriarch of Chuzhou circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year he became commanding myriarch of Chuzhou.

sentences.zh: 二十二年，還冠氏，卒，年五十七。

translations.literal: In the twenty-second year he returned to Guan Prefecture and died, aged fifty-seven.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-second year he returned to Guan and died at fifty-seven.
